utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI-WHYTE
utterances.text: Morning ladies and gentlemen. We are back after a fortnight; no vacation, really. The fort- night absence from active duty in the Trial Chamber. So we are now going to continue from where we stopped. Can we have the appearances.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: For the prosecution. My name is Mr. Niemann and I appear with Ms. McHenry, Mr. Turone and Ms. Ellis Van Dusschoten.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Good morning your Honours, I am Edina Residovic defence counsel for Zejnil Delalic. My colleague is Eugene O'Sullivan.

utterances.speaker: MR. OLUJIC
utterances.text: I am Zejnil Olujic for Zdravko Mucic. My colleague is Michael Greaves, Attorney from the United Kingdom of Great Britain and Northern Ireland. MR.. KARABDIC: Good morning your Honours, I am Salih Karabdic, Attorney from Sarajevo, Attorney for Hazim Delic. With me is Tom Moran, lawyer from Houston, Texas.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: Good morning your Honours. I am John Ackerman and my co-counsel is Cynthia McMurrey from the United States. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORAN
utterances.text: We are having a little difficulty getting the transcript on these computers. If the technical folks could take a look at it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI-WHYTE
utterances.text: I am sure someone will be able to check on them.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI-WHYTE
utterances.text: Mr. Niemann.

utterances.speaker: MR. TURONE
utterances.text: Good morning your Honours, our next witness was supposed to be protected from the media and the public but he gave up this protection. So he will testify in open court. We call Mr. Milenko Kuljanin as our next witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI-WHYTE
utterances.text: Yes, bring the witness in.

utterances.speaker: MR. O'SULLIVAN
utterances.text: Your Honours perhaps before the witness starts to testify we should get the computer transcript correct. It is still not done yet.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI-WHYTE
utterances.text: Kindly ask the witness to wait. The Trial Chamber will rise for a few minutes and immediately we know everything is all right we will come in.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORAN
utterances.text: Thank you your Honour (The witness enters court).

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI-WHYTE
utterances.text: Would you kindly put the witness on oath (Milenko Kuljanin, sworn).

utterances.speaker: MR. TURONE
utterances.text: May I proceed, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI-WHYTE
utterances.text: Yes, you can.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: May I start, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you please state your full name, sir?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Milenko Kuljanin.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What is your date of birth, Mr.. Kuljanin?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: 1st February 1968.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What is your ethnic group?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I am a Serb.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Where were you born?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Konjic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Kuljanin, what education did you receive, I mean what kind of schools did you attend?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I completed secondary school for catering in Sarajevo.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What was your profession in 1992?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I was a waiter.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Where did you live at the beginning of May 1992?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I lived in Bradina.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was there a time when Bradina was affected by the armed conflict in 1992?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you say on which date did that happen?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Bradina was attacked on 25th May 1992 by the Muslim and Croat paramilitary formations.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was there a time then when you were arrested?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I was captured, arrested on 29th or 30th May 1992 by the Muslim, as I described them, paramilitary formations in the village of Ljuta near Kalinovik.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you say very briefly the circumstances of your arrest and what happened right after your arrest?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Before I was arrested the village of Bradina was attacked by the Muslim and Croat paramilitary formations. They attacked the virtually unarmed population that happened to be in Bradina. They started setting fire to houses, shooting at the people that they encountered and killing them and with a couple of friends I tried to escape from the onslaught of Muslim and Croat. I do not know how to call them myself, and I went -- I sought shelter and finally I was captured and arrested in the village of Ljuta not far from Kalinovik. When we were arrested we were mistreated in various ways. We were tortured in the village of Ljuta itself where we were arrested. After that they transferred us to Mount Igman, where they beat us again and mistreated us. We were kept there for some time and then we were transferred to the camp to the Celebici camp. In the Celebici camp they beat us as soon as we arrived. They lined us up against the wall.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Kuljanin, just a moment: going back to the time of your arrest, how many were the soldiers who arrested you, approximately?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: There were about 50, 50 soldiers.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you say to which military units did they belong?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: They were Muslim paramilitary units.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you observe which uniforms did they wear and any insignia they might have had?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, they were wearing uniforms with the insignia of the lillies that they had and still have.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How many people were arrested together with you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: 20 odd people were arrested.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were you told why you were being arrested?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: We were told because we were Serbs. That is the one and only reason that they arrested us, kill us, mistreated us and tortured us. In view of the fact that we had not killed anyone, we did not attack anyone, we were in our homes where we lived and so on.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Kuljanin, did you reach Celebici camp with a vehicle, I suppose; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, we arrived in the Celebici camp on board a military vehicle of FAP make. On this military vehicle we were tied up, we were beaten. During the drive to the Celebici camp and the guard who was sitting on top fired at us and on that occasion he killed one of the prisoners and wounded four.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Kuljanin, can you say on which day you arrived at Celebici and approximately at what time in the day?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I cannot say exactly because I do not remember, but I think it was late in the afternoon.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What day, of what date?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The 29th, 30th; I cannot recall exactly.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Mr. Kuljanin, did you have any weapon yourself at the time of your arrest?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, I did not.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you in any way take part in the defence of the village of Bradina?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Unfortunately I did not.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you approximately say whether there were persons in Bradina and how many persons in Bradina who were armed and took part in some defence of the village?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: There must have been armed people, if there had been armed people in Bradina it would not have suffered the fate it did, which means that they were not armed, except for perhaps a hunting rifle or would or some small arms that people might have had like a pistol. I am not aware of any other arms.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Kuljanin, would you now tell us in detail what happened to you right after your arrival at Celebici?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: After we arrived in Celebici we were shut up in tunnel number nine. Before we entered this tunnel we had to stand up against a wall for several hours and while we were standing there the guards, the soldiers who were there, they beat us, they hit us, killed us. After that we were put in tunnel number nine, where our suffering continued. They tortured us in all kinds of possible ways. As for the tunnel itself --

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Just a moment, Mr. Kuljanin, you said you were lined up against a wall together with the other ones, were you personally beaten in this occasion while being lined up at the wall?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I was. They beat me.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How long about were you beaten?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: They beat me because I had only just been captured. I did not know any of the guards by name. So I did not know who it was at first. I do not know who beat me when we had only just arrived.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But my question was; how long were you beaten in this occasion. Did you not hear me?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: For how long were you beaten on that occasion while you were lined up at the wall? Do you hear the translation?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I hear now. I did not hear a moment ago. I only just managed to hear. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So my question was; for how long were you beaten at the wall in this occasion?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: For about three or four hours.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did anybody take note of your names right after your arrival at Celebici?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: When we arrived in Celebici and before being lined up against the wall in the command, when we were tied up and they took down their names. That was all. After that they started beating us. This beating went on for three or four hours after which we were put in the tunnel.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Mr. Kuljanin, you see a model in front of you in this courtroom. You can stand up and watch it and look at it if you wish. My question is; do you recognise what does the model represent first of all?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It is the model of the Celebici camp.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So, could you please indicate, may I ask the usher to provide the witness with something to point, could you indicate on the model the places you have been talking so far. I mean the entrance of the camp, the wall where you were lined up and tunnel number nine. If you want to turn around the model you can, of course?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The entrance to the camp was here. The gate was here, (indicating) there was the command building, the Infirmary (indicating) tunnel number nine, hangars number six (indicating). These were also hangars (indicating). The manhole was here, (indicating) a manhole.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right, thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: And some other buildings over here.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You can go back to your seat. Now, Mr. Kuljanin, in which physical conditions were you when you first entered tunnel nine?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I was in a poor physical condition because we had been beaten en route to the camp and at the camp when we arrived there. I was in a very poor physical condition.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you receive any medical care?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, we did not.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you first entered tunnel nine were there any prisoners already inside the tunnel?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: When we entered tunnel number nine there were no prisoners inside. It was empty.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you please now describe the physical characteristics of tunnel nine; give us a description of tunnel nine?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Tunnel number nine was underground. It was about 1 metre and 20 centimetres wide in my assessment, and about 20 metres long. In fact, as I said it was under the ground and it was an incline. I am not sure what the degrees of the gradient were.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Was there any electric light inside the tunnel?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The electric lights were never turned on. There were electric lights but they were never turned on during our stay in the tunnel.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was there any natural light? I mean, was there any opening through which daylight could enter into the tunnel?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, at the entrance door, but very little. From around half of the tunnel it was pitch dark. You could only see halfway towards the door.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Kuljanin, how long did you stay in tunnel nine?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: In tunnel number nine I stayed for about 110 days.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I understand that when you arrived there you were about 20 people; did the number of prisoners in number nine change in the period of time you remained there?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, it did. The number of prisoners kept increasing in tunnel number nine. They kept bringing new people from the neighbouring villages. They brought or neighbours. The number of people in tunnel nine increased to around 40, if I recall correctly.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you sit in a particular place inside the tunnel?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: In tunnel number nine I sat by the door. I was the sixth or seventh from the door.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you now tell you how were the conditions of life in tunnel nine, I mean, food, drinking water, toilet facilities, where did you sleep, etc?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: We slept in the tunnel. We slept in the tunnel, the conditions were extremely poor. It will suffice to take a look at the tunnel, that is sufficient in itself. As regard food and water and all other conditions, they were very poor. We only received every third day a slice of bread. We would receive a loaf of bread for 13 or 17 of us depending from practically day-to-day. The same goes as far as water. As far as relieving ourselves. We did to do it in the tunnel and it was horrendous. The conditions in fact were abominable, as the tunnel itself shows.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What about the toilet facility, how did you manage?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: We had to relieve ourselves in the tunnel itself. There was a bucket which was thrown in by the Muslim guards and we had to use that to relieve ourselves in. That was our toilet.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were you also allowed sometimes to go out to relieve yourself?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, they would let us out to relieve ourselves sometimes, but before we relieved ourselves, we had to stand next to the wall, raise our arms and spread our legs so that Hazim Delic would hit each of us with a baseball bat two or three times on the back, on the kidneys. It was only then that we were allowed to relieve ourselves. After that we would return to the tunnel.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: May I ask the usher to provide the witness with production exhibit number 1, which is a set of photos of the camp. I would like the witness to see on the ELMO, please, photo 45 first on page 33, I suppose. Mr. Kuljanin, do you recognise anything in this photo?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I do. This is tunnel number nine.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes, could you please now look at the following photo, number 46, please.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: That is probably not reentered the right way on the ELMO. Yes, that is correct.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: This is the interior of the tunnel, tunnel number nine.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. What about the next photo, number 47?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That is the rear end of tunnel number nine.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Production exhibit No. 1, so far we do not need it now but we will need it again later. So, Mr. Kuljanin, after the beating you suffered the very first day at the wall, were you personally beaten again during the period of your stay in tunnel nine?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I was beaten many times.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So without giving --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: By --

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: -- Giving any detail yet, can you say approximately how frequently were you personally beaten during your stay in tunnel nine?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Three to four times personally, not to mention the mass beatings, when I was beaten with the rest. I was personally beaten three or four times.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Again without giving any detail yet, did you personally suffer any other physical maltreatment besides beating during the period of your stay in tunnel nine?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did that happen once or more than once?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It happened two times.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So now, can you help describe in detail every single major incident. I mean every major incidents either beaten or maltreated that you personally suffered while you were in tunnel nine, please?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, now I would mention the maltreating and the torture by Landzo, who came to the door and asked me if I was married read etc. As I said, I was not married. He told me what if I take you to watch a cassette, this was a cassette of a wedding of a relative of mine where I was a member of the wedding party. He could not understand some of those things. So he took me out with Osman Dedic, Camdzic and I cannot remember the names of the others. He tied me up. He tied me to a pole and also gagged me. He ordered me to kneel, and as I kneeled -- when I kneeled they started to beat me. They beat me with rifle butts. They kicked me with their feet. They hit me with sticks. I do not remember all manner of thing they beat me with. They were strong blows and I hurt terribly. I fell down. I almost lost consciousness. When they stopped beating me and torturing me I was unable to get up. He then called the other two guys from tunnel number nine, other two guys from tunnel nine took me in.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you say he called, who do you mean he called?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Landzo, whom I already mentioned. I told you what he had asked me. Then I would also like to mention the torture I suffered at the hands of Hazim.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Before you go to another incident, I would like to focus on this one, Mr. Kuljanin. By whom exactly were you tied to the pole?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: By Landzo, I was tied to the pole by Landzo.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you remember where in the camp was this pole?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It was above the tunnel number nine.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: May I invite you, Mr. Kuljanin, to look again at the photos you have on your right-hand side on the ELMO beside you and look at these photos just to find out, if you find in these photos the pole which might be the one that you are talking about. Can you indicate?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: (Indicating).

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was that the pole that you were tied to?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were you also gagged with something within you were tied to the pole?

utterances.speaker: MR. MORAN
utterances.text: Excuse me, your Honour.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I have already said that I was gagged by Landzo. He gagged me and he tied me to the pole. They ordered me to kneel, then they started to beat me with rifle butts and hit me with all sorts of things.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: For the record I will say that the witness indicated photo number 50 in prosecution exhibit No 1. Thank you. So, with what were you beaten while you were tied to the pole?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: As I have already mentioned, I was viciously beaten by rifle butts, by some sorts of sticks. I was kicked, etc. They beat me until I almost lost consciousness. Then two came, two men came from tunnel number nine to bring me back inside, to take me back inside because I could not do it myself.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How long did all this last, approximately?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It lasted from half an hour to 45 minutes approximately, if not more.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you remember approximately when did this happen, at least in which month?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It happened somewhere in June, some time in June. I cannot remember the date.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. So can you help now describe any other incident you personally suffered during the period you stayed in tunnel nine. Pass to next incident please?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I can refer to an incident which where Hazim Delic was the perpetrator. He had this electrical gadget which he used to burn me twice. He put it to my chest on two occasions and I received an electric shock. Then I would also like to mention the occasions when he beat me with a baseball bat and kicked me --

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Kuljanin, before going to another incident let us focus, please, on the one concerning the electrical device. Can you please describe in detail this electrical device?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Delic entered tunnel number nine with this device which I already mentioned. Then he put it to my chest twice and I do not know how it functioned but I received two electrical shocks. It was horrible and unpleasant.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Kuljanin, my question is could you please give us a physical description of this electrical device? Did how did it look like? How was it done?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I can.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Please do that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: This electrical device had the form of a packet of cigarettes but it was much larger. On top it had two wires. There was a button on the device approximately, a connecting button so that the wires would conduct electricity to the chest so that I would receive a shock and the shock which I did receive was terribly unpleasant. I had convulsion on account of the shock and I twitched.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you mean Mr. Delic used the electrical device on you twice in the same day or on different days?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Twice on the same day.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did he apply this device on your skin or on your clothes?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: He applied it on my skin.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Exactly on which part of your body?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The chest, below the neck.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did any visible traces remain on your skin after that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, initially there was a trace and it remained there for three or four months. They were spots where the wires had contacted the skin. They were tiny scars on account of the contact with the electricity.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did Delic use this device on you inside the tunnel?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: He used it inside the tunnel.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did he say anything while using this device on you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, he laughed. He found it funny.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you say approximately when did this happen, at least in which month?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It happened approximately in July, the month of July.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you ever see Mr. Delic using this device on anybody else besides you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I did. It happened in the tunnel, he applied this device also to other prisoners who were in the tunnel with me.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you say approximately how many times and can you say the names of any of these prisoners who received this treatment?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I can state some of the names of the people who were subjected to this form of torture and maltreatment. They are Desimir Mrkajic, Radovan Dordic, Marko Kuljanin, Kuljanin Radovan and these I can remember.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right, thank you. Did you ever hear Mr. Delic saying anything to any of these prisoners while using the electrical device on them?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: With some of them he talked during this and laughed at them as he was applying the device. Some of them begged him as they were in pain and unpleasant pain not to do that not to torture them, not to maltreat them, but he even hit some of them when they begged him to cease torturing them. He merely laughed.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right, Mr. Kuljanin. Now you were going to talk about another incident and you mentioned something like a baseball bat. Could you go on on this account?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, your Honour I can continue. Delic that baseball bat which he used the most, I have personally felt if on my skin. I was personally maltreated by Delic with a baseball bat in the tunnel and in front of the tunnel. He would enter the tunnel. He entered the tunnel with a baseball bat. I was sitting inside and he started walking me on the back with it and on the kidneys specifically. Then he would take me out in front of the tunnel and I stood against the wall. I had to raise my arms and spread my legs. They he hit me also with the baseball bat on the back and on the kidneys.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Approximately how many times did Delic beat you with this baseball bat?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: He hit me many times, lot of times.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Kuljanin, did Mr. Delic say anything to you while beating you with the baseball bat?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: He did. He mentioned Serbian, he mentioned the Chetniks. It mainly all boiled down to the fact that we were Serbs and he said as much. In fact there existed no other reason.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you ever see Mr. Delic using this baseball bat on other prisoners?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Oh, yes, I did. I saw him using the baseball bat on all the prisoners who were with me in tunnel number nine, on all the prisoners he used the baseball bat who were in tunnel number nine while I was there with all of them.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you say approximately how many times did that happen?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It happened virtually every day, almost every day.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you ever hear Mr. Delic say anything while beating any prisoner with this baseball bat?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, he would always have a reason. He would refer to the Chetniks, how the Chetniks were killing people. What they were doing to the Muslims - this and that. Those were his main pretext and his main excuses and reasons.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, Mr. Kuljanin, is there any other major incident that you probably suffered during the period you stayed in tunnel nine?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, when I was in tunnel number nine, Delalic and Mucic took us to the manhole where there was no air.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Excuse me, you said Delalic; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Delic, I said Delic. Delic and Mucic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes, what did they do?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: They took us to the manhole where there was no air. Delic came and ordered half of the men outside from tunnel number nine. Then they lined us up and we set out toward the direction. We were not aware then that we were heading for the manhole. Delic and Mucic were there as well as the guards escorting us, armed guards escorting us to the manhole without air. By the entrance to the manhole there stood Mucic. Mucic and Delic stood and we also had to run the gauntlet of guards before entering the manhole, who hit us in the manhole itself. It was very cramped and we were virtually one upon another. When we entered the manhole they closed it after. After some time there was no more air left in the manhole and the people inside started shouting and thumping on the lid to be opened from outside. We -- older people especially inside. Those outside were saying they would throw a bomb at us. We asked them to do that because it was intolerable inside. After eight hours we went out of the manhole. We were again beaten by the guards as we exited by Mucic Pavo and Delic Hazim. Mucic Pavo asked me as I was leaving the manhole about a guy I used to know, an acquaintance, in fact, and then after that we were returned to the tunnel, normally attended by beatings, etc.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Let us go to some specific question concerning this stay in the manhole. When you were called out of the tunnel, in order to go to the manhole how many other prisoners were called together with you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I think around 16 or 17 people. I think that was the figure. I am not quite sure. There may have been more or less.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you mention the names at least of some of the other prisoners?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I can mention some of the names of the prisoners who were with me in this manhole. There was Momir Mrkajic, Adelko Kuljanin, Nikola Mrkajic, Branislav Mrkajic, Jelenko Kuljanin, Rajko Doroic, Rajko Dordic, those are the names that I can recall.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: That is enough, thank you. Did you go to the manhole which you already indicate in the model walking or with some vehicle?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: On foot, lined up in a line, escorted by armed guards who beat us as we went along. They beat us as we entered the manhole.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Kuljanin, did Mr. Mucic and Mr. Delic walk together with you to the manhole?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, as I already said they moved with us towards the manhole and they stood outside the manhole while we entered and they were there also when we came out eight hours later, as I have already said.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Kuljanin, by whom, exactly, were you ordered to enter the manhole?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The orders were given by Hazim Delic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were all the guards who brought you to the manhole still present there when you entered the manhole?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, the guards formed a gauntlet that we had to run through and as we did they beat us with whatever they could lay hands on up to the very entrance into the manhole.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You told us the cover was closed, who closed the cover of the pit, of the manhole?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: One of the guards closed the lid on the pit.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So may I ask the witness to watch at photos, some photos in production exhibit No. 1 and precisely first photo number 38 first. Do you recognise anything in this picture. I think this is not the right picture, you know. Yes, this is picture 38. Do you recognise anything in this picture?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I do. This is the manhole.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you please go to photo number 39, please.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I can.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you recognise anything?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That is the entrance to the pit.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you please look at picture number 40. What is that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That is the manhole.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes. Photo number 41, please?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That is the appearance of the manhole inside, the internal appearance, the internal, an internal view of the manhole.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you now see photo number 42, please?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It is again a view of the manhole inside.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Kuljanin, how many prisoners were forced to enter the manhole?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I already said somewhere around 16 or 17, maybe more. They were all in this manhole and you see what it looks like.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How could they all fit in this manhole?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: We were all one on top of another, like sardines in a box, all one on top of another, virtually thrown one upon another.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you say where exactly you were inside the manhole, I mean were you down on the floor or over other prisoners?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I was on the floor, actually and the other prisoners were standing on my back on top of me. Some of them were leaning with their hands against me because, as I just said, we were all one on top of another. It was a small manhole for all these people to fit. The actual appearance of the manhole as you can see was such that there were also pipes around it, so it was virtually impossible for all of us to fit in, but we did.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you breathe normally inside there?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, the manhole was almost automatically closed. There was just a pipe that appeared in the surface and some air could pass through. After some time, a guards who was on the outside he shut this pipe to prevent the air from coming in. After some time people started to panic, there was no air is there. They started begging the guard to open the lids but he refused. He even threatened to throw a grenades into the manhole. At the end we begged him to do that because we just could not go on like that. There was no air; we could not breathe.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Kuljanin, you said you remained inside this manhole about eight hours. Did any of the prisoners lose consciousness during these eight hours?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, two. They were not quite unconscious but almost. When the lid was opened we all started climbing out an they stayed inside. Then we shook them a little. They came too and then they came out too.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know whether any of the guards remained outside of the manhole while you were in all the time?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, a guard who was on the lid all the time throughout the eight hours that we were in the manhole. He was sitting there, and I said we had to beat on the lid, begging him to let us get some air, but he threatened to throw a bomb, as I had said, and as we could not stand it any more we begged him to do that, but eventually the lids opened and we came out.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know the name of this guard who remained there the whole time?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I only know his nickname. He was known as Karavan.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How many guards did you see there when you could get out of the manhole?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I cannot tell you the exact number, but there were quite a number of guards. Again they made a gauntlet and we had to pass through it,. And Delic and Mucic stood there watching them mistreating us as we came out of the manhole.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You say Mr. Mucic told you something at this time; can you say exactly what did he tell you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, he did. Mucic asked me about somebody whom he probably knew. He asked me where he was, how he was. I answered that I did not know, and he said that he would come soon as well and that he would go to the manhole again. He mentioned Snjezan. This man was not in the camp but he said he would be joining us soon, but he did not come, this young man. That was the question that he asked me. That was the whole conversation that we did at that time.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you then go back to tunnel nine?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, when we came out of the manhole we were returned to tunnel number nine. When we went back, the other prisoners went out and we assumed that they would be taken to the manhole as well. The Group that was taken out after us was taken to the manhole, but among those who were in the manhole with me was Rajko Djordjic and he was taken with the second Group again and when he was told that he would be going there again. He begged Mucic and Delic to kill him rather than put him back in the manhole, but they would not listen and Rajko Djordjic was back in the manhole with a second Group that spent even more than eight hours, more time than my Group had spent in it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So when did the prisoners of the second Group come back?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I cannot tell the exact time, but I know that they spent more time there than the first Group.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: After these prisoners came back did any of them tell you where they were brought?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, they told us.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What did they tell you and who?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Rajko Djordjic, as he was sitting next to me as I had mentioned, he was in the first Group and in the second. So he told me that they had spent time in the manhole and that it was worse than the first time because they were kept there longer and people were losing consciousness, even more so than in the first Group and that the same procedure was followed. The gauntlet, the beating, everything.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. So Mr. Kuljanin, approximately when did all this happen, the manhole incident, at least in which month did that happen?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I think it was in July.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right, Mr. Kuljanin, is there any other incident that you personally suffered during the period of your stay in tunnel nine, I mean any other major incident you have to describe while you stayed in tunnel nine?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The main incident has to do with the killings that occurred in tunnel number nine.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I am asking you about incidents you personally suffered, maltreatment, you probably suffered while you stayed in tunnel nine. Do you have anything else to add to what you said so far about what you suffered probably while you were in tunnel nine?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I was mistreated every single day by Landzo, by Delic and the other guards. They would take us out daily, me personally and beat us, together with other prisoners, in front of the tunnel and inside the tunnel. This was more or less every day.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Did you receive any medical care in the whole period you spent in tunnel nine?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Throughout my stay in tunnel number nine and tunnel number six we did not receive, I did not receive any kind of medical treatment.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: As far as you know and as far as you might have seen, did any other prisoner receive any medical care?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Not a single person that was with me in tunnel number nine was given any kind of medical aid or treatment. There were people who lost an eye, with broken arms, with broken legs and no medical treatment whatsoever was given to them.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right, Mr. Kuljanin, you were mentioning something about killings. So did you personally observe any grave mistreatment of any other prisoner while you were in tunnel nine and in particular do you know anything because of direct knowledge about the circumstances of the death of any prisoner inside the camp?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes. If I may mention the mistreatment of other prisoners Nikola Mrkajic Sukasic and Djordje Djordjic. They were tortured by Delic and Landzo.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORAN
utterances.text: Your Honour, this is not in response to the question.

utterances.speaker: MR. TURONE
utterances.text: I would say this is a response, your Honour. I asked him: "What did you personally observe of any other grave mistreatment of any other prisoners while you were in tunnel nine and, in particular, do you know anything because of direct knowledge about the circumstances of the death?" So I am asking the witness about mistreatments he might have eyewitnessed, not only mistreatments ending with the death, but in any case.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI-WHYTE
utterances.text: He said --

utterances.speaker: MR. TURONE
utterances.text: He said he, "I personally".

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI-WHYTE
utterances.text: He said he understood, not that he witnessed.

utterances.speaker: MR. TURONE
utterances.text: I believe that this witness eyewitnessed a number of incidents concerning other prisoners.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI-WHYTE
utterances.text: Are you giving the evidence of what he said? He has already said what he --

utterances.speaker: MR. TURONE
utterances.text: I am assuming that the witness has to be allowed to give the account of what he personally saw with his eyes. I suppose he will.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI-WHYTE
utterances.text: I am sorry, you were not listening. If you were listening you would have heard. He said: "I understood certain persons were tortured". That is what he said.

utterances.speaker: MR. TURONE
utterances.text: All right, Mr. Kuljanin. Please give us the accounts of what you saw with your eyes concerning mistreatments suffered by other prisoners while you were in tunnel nine, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI-WHYTE
utterances.text: Kindly let us hear only what you saw or what you heard.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I want to tell you what I saw, that is what I have been saying. I have been talking only about what I saw, and I mentioned two people who were mistreated by Delic and Landzo. May I do that, may I talk about that?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI-WHYTE
utterances.text: Yes, this is what you are expected to talk about.

utterances.speaker: MR. TURONE
utterances.text: Go on, Mr. Kuljanin, please.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: As regards Vukasin Mrkajic, he came to tunnel number nine with broken ribs on both sides of his chest. Those ribs were fractured by Delic. In the tunnel itself Delic would come every day, as he had swellings on both sides because of these broken ribs Delic would hit him against those ribs to hurt him. Then I would mention the torture of Rajko Djordjic by Delic and Landzo who tortured, beat him, beat him up with sticks, with baseball bats, with their boots, who shut him up in the manholes without water, etc etc. This could be testified by all the prisoners who were in number nine because these mistreatments were repeated almost daily. They would take us out to sunbathe, allegedly. They would tell us to strip up to our waist, to line us up against a wall next to tunnel number nine. We had to stand apart, raise our arms behind our heads. Then Delic would come with a baseball bat, escorted by guards, who would follow him. Then he would hit us, then the guards would hit us until we fell unconscious. Then they would shove us back into tunnel number nine.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right, Mr. Kuljanin. Do you know anything because of direct knowledge, observation about the circumstances of the death of any prisoner inside the camp?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I can mention two killings in the camp that I personally eyewitnessed. I would first like to mention the killing of Slavko Susic carried out by Senad Landzo and Hazim Delic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: In the case of Slavko Susic, he was born in Celebici, the place where the camp itself was situated. Slavko Susic was brought to tunnel number nine maybe a month after us and he was brought to the tunnel by Delic, who followed him in, who beat him to the very entrance and inside as well. Delic beat him with a rubber pole somewhere halfway into the tunnel. Slavko was all covered in blood. He was swollen. His eyelids were swollen. Delic left him in tunnel number nine. He went out and he ordered Zarko Mrkajic to investigate Slavko Susic in connection with a radio transmitter that only he knew about, claiming that Slavko Susic had this radio transmitter, receiver. Zarko Mrkatic questioned him, talked to him nicely. He asked him whether he had this radio transmitter. He said that he had no idea about it, that he did not have one. However, Delic came back two or three hours later, I cannot say exactly after how much time, and he asked Zarko whether he had confessed to having this radio transmitter. As he did not have one he could not confess. Delic took Zarko out demanding that he confess about this radio transmitter. When this did not help Delic took Slavko out, beat him and who knows what else he did to him, but then he came into the tunnel and he said that he had admitted that he had a radio transmitter and that he was going with him to his home to bring back this radio transmitter. They went and returned without a radio transmitter because the man did not have one. Anyway Delic started hitting him again and said that he was lying, that he was cheating, that he did have a radio station but he refused to admit. This beating went on, or rather Delic beat him. Then he shoved him back into tunnel number nine. Then Landzo came, Zenga. He took him out in front of tunnel number nine. He pulled his tongue with pliers. He wrapped a fuse round his leg and his waist, setting light to it, forcing the man to admit something that he could not admit because he simply did not have such a radio transmitter. Zenga set light to the fuse. The man was burning. He tortured him in various ways. When Zenga stopped with this torture, Slavko Susic crawled on his -- on all fours into the tunnel because he simply could no longer walk. Slavko Susic stayed there, spent the night. I think the next day Delic continued torturing him and beating him and that same day about 4 or 5 the man succumbed to this torture and passed away. Slavko Susic lay there dead. After he had died the prisoners who were sitting close to him, they dragged him near the door and positioned him in the proper position for a dead man. He was left there for two nights and a day, after which Delic and Zenga and the guards came and accused us that we had killed Slavko Susic, after which they continued to mistreat and beat us because they had killed Slavko Susic, but they said that we had killed him, adding that: "See what you have done to one of your own, imagine what you would do to the Muslims." Slavko Susic's body lay there for two nights and a day after which he was taken away. What happened to him, he was probably thrown away somewhere. I have no idea what happened to his body.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right, Mr. Kuljanin, may we have some specific questions on this incident concerning Slavko Susic?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI-WHYTE
utterances.text: Actually, I would rather let us start with a break and come back at 12, so that we will continue then.

utterances.speaker: MR. TURONE
utterances.text: All right, your Honour (Short adjournment). (12 o'clock).

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI-WHYTE
utterances.text: Please remind the witness he is still under his oath.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: May I remind you that you are still under oath?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TURONE
utterances.text: May I proceed?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI-WHYTE
utterances.text: Yes, you can.

utterances.speaker: MR. TURONE
utterances.text: So Mr. Kuljanin, let us go to some specific questions concerning the incident having to do with Slavko Susic. You say that Mr. Susic first appeared in the tunnel one day, approximately one month after your arrival. Can you say approximately at what time of the day did he arrive, that very first day you saw him in the tunnel?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I think that it was in the morning, as far as I remember.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You say that Mr. Delic came and invited Zara Mrkajic to interrogate Mr. Susic; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, that is correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you remember what did you hear Delic saying too Zara Mrkajic exactly?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That he was to interrogate him on account of a radio transmitter and that he had to confess where it was and that he knew everything that Susic had confessed. Normally Susic had admitted nothing because he did not have a radio transmitter. He did not know of any radio transmitter so he admitted nothing of the kind.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You said after that Mr. Delic came back and questioned Zara Mrkajic about the results of his interrogation; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, and he also beat Zara so as to force him to admit something that -- to having something he did not have. When that did not help, I have already said this, I do not know if I need repeat this, what happened then.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes, but did Delic say anything else and ask anything else from Zara after this?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: He asked whether he had. The man had confessed and he beat Zara so that Zara would interrogate him again and make him confess and admit to having something that he did not have, as I have already repeated thrice. Then Delic came and took him out and he was out with him. Then he returned to the tunnel and said that he confessed to having a radio transmitter at home. So they went to him, his home. They went there, stayed there some time and, of course, they did not find one. He said he was cheating and lying and that he would remember that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did this visit to the house of Mr. Susic take place the same day or the following morning?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It took place on the next day, this visit.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you mean in the morning or in the afternoon?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: In the morning, around 9 o'clock.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So, around 9 o'clock, did Delic come back to the tunnel?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I think so, with Susic. He did, he did, after he had gone to the house with him, allegedly to get the radio transmitter. Then he returned with him to the tunnel and beat him in the tunnel and the other man fell in the tunnel and he went there without any results.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When they came back from the house of Susic, do you remember having heard something which Delic said before beating Susic in the tunnel?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: He kept accusing him because of the radio transmitter and beating him because of the radio transmitter and the man had no idea what he was talking about. After his death, after Susic had been killed and after he had been taken away -- I do not know where, I do not know where they had thrown him -- Delic came back and in front of all of us who were there incarcerated in tunnel number nine, he said: "Let me tell you something, from my private life." He said that allegedly his grandfather in his village in the time of the Second World War had killed several people and that he had taken revenge upon Susic for that, and Susic ended the way that he had. That is all that he said in connection with Susic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Going back to this morning when Delic and Susic came back from the house of Susic, with what did Delic beat Susic inside the tunnel on this occasion?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: He beat him with some sort of a rubber stick.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: For how long did he beat him on this occasion?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: He beat him in the tunnel, starting from the door and then halfway inside the tunnel until he fell. Then he left.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You said that later on Zenga came; can you say at approximately what time of this day did Zenga come?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Well, as we had a very poor sense of orientation in terms of time of day and dates, I really cannot remember exactly the time and the exact hour when this took place. I cannot remember.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. You said something about Zenga using pliers with the tongue of Mr. Susic; what did Zenga do with the tongue of Mr. Susic as far as you could see?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: He pulled out the tongue, his tongue, with pliers and twisted it. Then he used later a slow burning fuse to torture him with, as I have already described. I do not know whether I need repeat that. Of course, I can do that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I just have some specific questions: you were talking about fuse around the leg and around the waist?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you describe exactly what did Zenga do with this fuse or fuses? How many fuses were there - one or two different fuses?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: There were two fuses which were the same. He put one around his leg and one around his belly under the shirt. Then he ignited them. Of course it started burning the man's skin and he started screaming and begging him to take them off. However, the fuse burned and did the damage it did, burning the man's skin.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How did Mr. Landzo fix the fuses to the body? Did he fix them in some way or simply wrap them?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: On the leg he fastened them with some Scotch tape, I believe, and as regards the one around the belly, he just wrapped it under his shirt.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So the fuses were wrapped around the skin, not over the clothes; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, around the skin.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How did Zenga light the two fuses, with what?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: He had a match box and he used a match to ignite the fuses. They normally started burning, and affecting the body.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did the fuses around Susic's leg and waist burn entirely or were they put off?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, they burnt entirely.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What did Zenga do in the meantime?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: In the meantime, while the fuse was burning, he hit the man.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: With what?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: He kicked him and he also hit him with the rifle butt.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did Mr. Landzo say anything while beating him during this treatment?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: He asked him about the radio transmitter and kept insisting that he say where it was, but he obviously could not; and then he faired as he did.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Approximately how long did this treatment last?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Certainly over 45 minutes, the burnings, the torture and the pulling out of the tongue, in my assessment, perhaps a bit longer.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could Mr. Susic move by himself after this treatment?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: After Zenga's treatment, Landzo's treatment, that is, Susic crawled on all-fours towards the place where he had been sitting before in the rear of the tunnel, and he crawled back to that place on all-fours.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How long did Mr. Susic remain at his place after this treatment?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Mr. Susic, I am not quite sure of the time, but he stayed there until Delic came, and when he came, he started beating and maltreating him again and maltreating him again about the radio transmitter. The man could not even speak. He could not seen scream because he was on the verge of death, as it were. Then he stopped after. They stopped beating him. He died after a couple of hours. The prisoners, when they saw that he was showing no signs of life, took him to the front end of the tunnel and there placed him in a position befitting a dead man.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes, you said this already, Mr. Kuljanin. Do you mean Mr. Delic beat Susic inside the tunnel in the place where Susic was sitting?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes. Let me just go back to the beginning, before Susic came to the tunnel and before his death and all this torture he had already been beaten black and blue and bloody and swollen before he had come to the tunnel. This all took place in the tunnel, and in front of the tunnel, in front of the tunnel Landzo tortured him and inside the tunnel Delic did.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I am talking about the last time Delic beat Susic inside the tunnel?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did Delic say anything before beating Susic and during the beating, I mean, during this last beating?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, he did. He said that the Chetnik would not confess to having a radio station and to having guided shells to Celebici. In fact, I did not hear of a single shell landing at Celebici, but allegedly this man had been guiding them.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When did you realise that Susic was dead?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I realised that when these people who were sitting near him said that he was dead, that he was not showing signs of life any longer. Then this news was transmitted from prisoner to prisoner and I could definitively see he was dead when they brought him to the front end of the tunnel, where he lay for two days unmoving or, rather, dead.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So you mean that the body lay on the floor of the tunnel right near you; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, right in front of me. My legs were over his body.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. So, could you personally observe that Susic did not have any sign of life any more, was motionless?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, he was rigid. He was stiff for two days and two nights. He was obviously rigid.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You said the body remained there for a couple of days; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, two days and two nights. It was completely blue, as if he had taken an ink bath.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What injuries were visible on the body, as far as you could see?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: As I have already stated, he was bruised and blue, and he had a cut on his lips, probably from the pliers with which his tongue had been pulled out. In addition to that, his eyes were totally swollen and shut from the blows normally.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Kuljanin, were the burns visible on the leg and on the waist?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, they were visible, quite conspicuous in fact, the burns on the leg and on the body elsewhere, and the shirt which he had been wearing was torn.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: After the body of Susic was finally removed, did you ever see it again after that or never again?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, never again did I see that body.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. So, this is, I would say, the end of the Susic's incident. Did you eyewitness any other incident concerning any other prisoner who died?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I would like to mention the murder, the killing of Zeljko Milosevic. I should also like in that connection to mention some journalists and the camera crew which came to the prison. I cannot remember exactly what country they had come from, but they came to film the prisoners, that is us. Delic called Rayko Dordzic and Zeljko Milosevic to be filmed by the camera and to tell the journalist and the TV crew and that took place in front of tunnel number nine, to tell them how they had tortured Muslim women and raped Muslim women and tortured and killed children, but Zeljko Milosevic would not admit anything of the kind and would not make any such statement on that score and Rajko Dordzic also could not confess to doing something that he had not done. Delic returned them to tunnel number nine, from which they had come, and when the journalists had left, he entered the tunnel again and said that they would remember him well. Zeljko, however, remained for another couple of days in the tunnel. Delic then came and told him to get ready around 1 pm. Then Delic came and called Milosevic. I cannot say exactly when he came. It was night. It was perhaps midnight or 2 o'clock am. It was pitch dark. He took Zeljko out personally. He called him to come out and took him out. After they had gone out, we heard Zeljko screaming and moaning and crying out. In the morning when they took us out to go to the toilet, Zeljko Milosevic was behind the door lying there dead. We saw him as we passed on our way to the toilet. But let me mention in this connection, before they kill him Zeljko Milosevic had been shut down in a manhole filled with water with Rajko Djordjic, where he had spent the whole night. When he returned from the manhole, he was soaking wet. I had a track suit, and as his clothes were wet, I gave him my track suite as a change of clothes so that he could put something dry on. Now to connect this to the murder, when I saw him he was wearing my track suit, and another, some sort of a parka, was also draped over his head. I recognised him and I could tell that it was Zeljko Milosevic by the fact that he was wearing that suit.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right, Mr. Kuljanin, let me ask some specific questions on this incident. Approximately when did this incident happen, at least in which month?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I spent around 110 days in the tunnel. All this took place during this 110 days which I spent there. Whether it was the beginning or July or the end of June, I cannot really tell. I do not orient myself really quite well, because we really, at least as far as I myself am concerned, cannot remember these more important dates because I could not orient myself in the space of time there. So I cannot say exactly. Possibly, it was the end of June or July, but his killing took place after Slavko Susic's incident.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: After the Slavko Susic's incident?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, after that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Where did Zeljko Milosevic sit inside the tunnel?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Zeljko Milosevic sat somewhere in the middle of the tunnel, halfway down the tunnel in the middle of the tunnel.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So you say that the night of his death he was called out by Mr. Delic in the night and you heard screaming. For how long did you hear screaming from outside?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, we heard him screaming for over an hour. I am not quite sure how long over an hour, but it was an hour at least and longer than that. So he had actually forewarned him of what was to come and told him to be ready at 1, and that was what happened.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You say that in the morning, going to the toilet outside you saw the body outside of the tunnel entrance. Did you see the body, both going to the toilet and coming back from the toilet?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, it was there on our way and when we were coming back to the tunnel, both times.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you say approximately how many minutes had passed between the time you saw the body while going to the toilet and the time you saw the body while coming back from the toilet?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: All this took place within the space of five or six minutes. Our time also was limited when it came to our going to the toilet.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was the body in the same position both times and was it motionless?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It was motionless and it was in the same position both times.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You say that you could recognise Milosevic by the garment you lent him, yes?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I recognise the Milosevic by the clothing which I had lent him and his sneakers which he used to wear when he was alive and when he stayed in the tunnel with the rest of us.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was the face of Mr. Milosevic covered?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: His face was covered up to his forehead. He was bald. He only had some hair on the back of his head and I also recognised him by that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Kuljanin, did you ever have a chance to see again Zeljko Milosevic or his body after this?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, no, I did not.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Now, did you personally -- did you ever see any of the guards coming to tunnel nine while you were there, beside the occasions you have been talking about so far?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I did not understand the question; if you would be kind to repeat it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you see the guards or any of the guards coming to tunnel nine while you were there on other occasions besides the occasions you have been already talking about until now?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, the guards stood at the door and some soldiers, some uniformed persons, would come in and beat us. They were people whom we did not know. The guards themselves did not come inside number nine often, but they did take us out in front of tunnel nine and beat us there because they did not have enough space inside.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right, thank you. So, Mr. Kuljanin, you said you stayed in the tunnel for about 100 to 120 days; did you stay in any other building inside the detention camp besides tunnel nine?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I stayed in hangar number six. Let me just mention one other thing which happened while I was still in tunnel number nine. As I have already said, there were around 30 to 40 of us prisoners in tunnel number nine. After 90 or 100 days Pavo Mucic came with some kind of a list and he singled out a number of the prisoners from tunnel number nine and he had them lined up in front of the tunnel. Thereafter, he transferred them to hangar number six. I remained in tunnel number nine with another 17 men and after this Hazim Delic, entered the tunnel number nine and said to us that we had been left there for the mine fields and that we would never leave the tunnel except when we head for the mine fields. Normally we thought that that would naturally be our fate, as we could not expect anything better in view of the treatment that we were receiving and the conditions that prevailed there. However, it did happen that we got out ourselves after 10 or 15 days out of tunnel number nine and were transferred ourselves to hangars number six as well.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So can you say approximately when did you move to hangar six, at least in what month?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I think it must have been September.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Who called you out of the tunnel in order to bring you to hangar six?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Mucic left us in the tunnel and one of the guards came to take us out from number nine and to transfer us to hangar number six. Who gave the orders, I really do not know, for this transfer to hangar number six, I do not know.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How long did you stay inside hangar six, approximately?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I stayed in hangar number six three, three-and-a-half, maybe four months, I am not quite sure. After which, I was transferred to the Musala camp in Konjic. When we were transferred to hangar number six, as I said, 17 of us, 17 prisoners, that same night the guards came, named Zilic and Camdzic were among them, and they started calling out names from the list of 17 people from number nine and to beat us. They beat us for several nights running, just those of us who had come from number nine. And they said that they were doing so under orders of the Command. I did not recognise many of the guards who were participating in this who were beating us during those nights, except for Landzo, Dedic and Camdzic. I could not recognise the others because it was nighttime and we had to face the wall against the hangar, so I could not see them.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you personally suffer any other physical maltreatment during your stay in hanger six?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I could mention one of those cases of maltreatment in hanger number six was when we were taken to steal some goods for Mucic from the neighbouring hangar, next to hangar number six. We were taken out of the hangars. I was taken out together with four other men during the night by Sejo -- I do not recall his surname -- and he took us to the neighbouring hangar where there was food. And we had to steal that food and we found hangar -- we found Mucic there. He ordered us to load this food on to his van and he transported those goods to his home with this van. We would go home with him and unload this stuff to his basement or garage. This happened twice. The first night that this took place we returned just before dawn to the hangars, I think it was about five o'clock. The guards came that night again and the four of us who went were beaten. Among the guards were Camdzic and Zilic. I do not recall the names of the others. When we went the second time to steal or to take, whichever you prefer, these goods, again it was night time, Sejo came and three others. I can give you the names. I remember Radovan Mr.sic, Relja Mrkajic and Radovan.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The doctor?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, no doctor, no. It was not the doctor and Radovan Mrkajic. That second night we were stealing again and when we -- the next night Hazim Delic came to the hangar and said those four who went on a tour the previous night should come out. We knew that he meant us, but we did not go out straight away. Then he called us out by name. When we went out, he ordered us to face the wall and he started beating us together with some other guards, whom I did not see. Those were some of the incidents I experienced with the exception of spades, with which Delic beat us, for instance, until we were virtually unconscious.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Kuljanin, let me ask you a specific question on these incident that you have been talking about right now. You have been talking about two visits to the house of Mr. Mucic with a van. Who was driving the van on these two occasions?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Mucic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Who was in the van besides Mucic?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: There was us, who went to steal the goods, to take those goods on his behalf, to steal them on his behalf, and the guards.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now let us talk about what happened after the second time when you said that the following evening Delic came and asked for the people who were on tower. What did Delic say exactly in this occasion?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: When we came out and when he started beating us together with the guards with him, he said that these blows, some were for the flowers, some were for the chocolate. He kept listing the things we had taken. I do not even remember. In any event, it was food stuffs that he was referring to, and as far as I could see.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: With what did they beat you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: They beat us with rifle butts, with their boots, with sticks.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How long did they beat you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: About half an hour, 40 minutes. They beat some more, some less; it depended.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What about these two occasions you brought food to the house of Mr. Mucic, were two occasions close to each other? How many days, how many...

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: A couple of days approximately in between.
