utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And, very approximately, when did all this happen, at least in which month?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, I really cannot remember what month it was.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right, never mind. So what else -- did you personally suffer any other physical maltreatment besides all this during your stay in hangar six?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, the perpetrator was Hazim Delic. He beat me with a shovel with his boots; he kicked me, all kinds of things; he took me out; he beat me inside; in addition, when he beat all of us with the shovel, together with his guards -- and the names I could mention is Camdzic and Zilic. This happened very frequently, almost every other day.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Is this all, was there any other incident you suffered personally while during the period of your stay in hangar six, is this all? You have some other incident to talk about?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: To tell you the truth, there were instances almost every day when Delic with his guards would hit us with shovels, with the handles of shovels. This was happening almost every day that we were staying, that we stayed in hangars number six in Celebici.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was there any other time you were called out of the hangar?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I could mention also, yes, when we were taken to clean up in front of Delalic's house. There were guards, security people, and a man in civilian clothes came in and pointed to four or five prisoners. I was one of them. He just pointed and we had to follow him. We did not know where we were going. When we got into the jeep that took us there, we arrived in Konjic in front of Delalic's house. It was raining and there was some sand and some stones there and we had to clean it up. With me was Dragan Dordic, Milan Gligorovic, Boran Mrkajic and Zeljko Kuljanin. When we arrived in front of Delalic's house there was very strong security. There was some close -- with crew cuts, there was some men with crew cuts and they were -- the men were saying to us that we would never be released, we would have to work for Delalic for as long as we lived. They were beating us all the time. We were clearing up there. They would beat us, kick us, they would say these things, threatening us that where he would never get out, that we would have to work for Delalic for as long as we lived.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Kuljanin, can you describe the place where they brought you, this house?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: They took us to the town of Konjic, where the house of the mentioned person was at the entrance to the town, the beginning of the town. That's where his house was. We had to clean up. We were mistreated and threatened and we took these threats very seriously.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I mean, can you describe this place with more detail? What was around the house?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The house, near the house is a hotel, across the street, a petrol station. Between the hotel and that house there is a parking lot. Next to the house is the Neretva river flowing. The house is on the main Mostar to Sarajevo road. That is the building.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How do you know this was the house of Mr. Delalic?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Actually, before the war, they there used to be a mechanics shop. Then there was a discotechque there that I used to go to. And I would drive there together with a colleague to that discotechque, so I knew it very well. I know exactly where it was and what it looked like.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know the first name of Mr. Delalic?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I do: Zejnil Delalic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How long did this cleaning last?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The cleaning lasted about three or four hours, four, something like that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How many guards were around the place there where you were cleaning up?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Well, roughly about 10 - 10 or so guards, well, armed guards, very well equipped, around the house and in front of the house.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were they in uniform?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, they were in uniform and well armed. It was like a combat equipment that they were wearing.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you say which kind of an uniform did they wear?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: They had camouflage uniforms, standard camouflage uniforms, with the insignia, their insignia with the lillies.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How did these guards treat you during the cleaning of the house?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I have already said that they hit us, that they beat us, that they threatened us, that they said that we would spend our life working for Delalic and that everything depended on him - our future fate depended on him.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you say with what did they beat you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: They kicked us an they beat us with rifles.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: At the end of it, who drove you back to Celebici?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: One of the soldiers who was there, they drove us back, he drove us back.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right, Mr. Kuljanin, did you know Mr. Delic from before the war?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: By sight.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you observe what official role did Mr. Delic have in the Celebici camp?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Delic's role was to stand in for Mucic when he was not there. He was the one who had the main say.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How did you get to know Mr. Delic's name?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I learnt of his name from the prisoners who were in tunnel number nine. Some of those prisoners had worked with Delic for years. They were colleagues, and that is how I learnt his name.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you describe physically, Mr. Delic?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I can. He is tall, bald, strong built, that is it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you know Mr. Landzo from before the war?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I did not know him from before the war. I met him at the camp itself.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How did you get to know Landzo's name and nickname "Zenga"?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: We heard others calling him by that name, his colleagues who helped him do the work he was doing.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you describe Mr. Landzo?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I can.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes, please do that.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: He was at the time in the camp, he was short, thin, with short hair, very short hair at the time while he was in the camp.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know what was the role of Mr. Mucic inside the Celebici camp?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: His role was, I think he was the commander, the manager. I do not know, but anyway his word meant a lot. He would make lists for the exchange and things like that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you see him --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: He would determine the groups.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you see him in the camp besides the two occasions you just mentioned?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I saw him quite a number of times.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Where in the camp did you see him?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Within the camp grounds. Very often he would drive a motorbike round the grounds. I would also see him coming by car. He was there very often. He would go to the command building. I would see him with a camera.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you remember very approximately when you saw Mr. Mucic for the first time, at least in which month?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I cannot remember. I cannot.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did Mr. Mucic use to wear a uniform?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you say which kind of a uniform?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: A camouflage uniform like all the others who were in the camp, including the guards and all the others.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you ever notice any insignia on his uniform?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Insignia, no, I did not see them.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did Mr. Mucic ever talk to you besides what you have already said?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: He did not talk to me. On one occasion he spoke to me in connection with an exchange. That was a very brief conversation and that was all I talked to him about.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right, Mr. Kuljanin. Were you ever interrogated by military investigators during your stay in Celebici?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: At the beginning.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Where in the camp did that happen?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: In the command building.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How many people did interrogate you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: There were two people who interrogated us and who escorted us to the office and stood as security while we were being investigated. Of course we were tied up.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you remember the names of these two people interrogating you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I do not remember their names.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were these two people in uniform?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, they were in uniform.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And was there a long interrogation?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: So so, half an hour.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How were you treated during the interrogation by these two people?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: During the interrogation they were very aggressive and rude. They would not accept anything that we said that did not suit them.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: By the way were you accused of anything specific by these two people?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I do not know, I have know idea. Obviously I must have been accused since I spent so much time there. They probably did. They charged me with my nationality. They had no other grounds.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What did they ask you, do you remember some questions they asked you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: For instance, are you a member of the SDS, are you a member of this, are you a member of that. All manner of things. I really do not remember the details.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What did you answer?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Talking about this question whether I was a member of the SDS. At that time I really was not. So I had no reason to hide it and I had no reason to say I was if I was not, but when I said that I was not a member of the SDS they started yelling and shouting saying "you are all members. You are all Chetniks," this and that. So they had to accept at the time that I was not a member of the SDS. I am today, I am a member and I am not concealing the fact.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was anybody typing a record during the interrogation?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: At the time no, no, there was no one.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: During the interrogation were your hands free or tied?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: We were tied. My hands were tied behind my back during the first interrogation.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, we will talk about the second occasion later on. So did anybody untie your hands during this interrogation?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, they did not.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were your hands tied with a rope or with handcuffs?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Some with wires, some with ropes. My hands were tied with wire.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you sign any piece of paper after that interrogation?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: A couple of days later I signed a piece of paper. I have no idea what it says on that paper.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So what happened a couple of days later? When did you go, when did you sign this piece of paper?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I cannot remember exactly how much later this was to the time when we made this statement, or rather we signed it without even reading it. I cannot remember how much time went by. Roughly three or four, maybe five days.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Kuljanin, my question is: where, in which place did you put your signature on this paper?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: At the bottom of the paper.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: No, no --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: In the command building. In the command building where we made the statement the first time.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So, were you brought to the command building again with hands tied behind the back or not?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, we were tied, but this time in front and not with wire, but with ropes this time.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did they untie your hands in order to have you sign the record?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Our hands were untied for us to sign the paper. Then they tied us up again until we were taken back to the tunnel.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you read the record before signing it?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, I did not.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was there any judicial proceedings against you after that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Against some there were judicial proceedings, but not against me.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. So Mr. Kuljanin, did the Red Cross ever visit the camp while you were in Celebici?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The Red Cross came several times to the Celebici camp.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What happened before, during and after these visits?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: When the Red Cross came for the first time to register us, to see us, we were so happy, so glad, but when the Red Cross left, when they departed from the camp, we were tortured so badly and persecuted that the next time they came we did not want to even look at them, not to mention speak to them because we had this terrible experience from their first visit, but the Red Cross promised that we would have no problems, that we would talk without the presence of the guards and the other staff of the camp, but when they left they continued beating us, saying that we had said this or that and all kinds of things. So that the second time we did not want, nor did we dare to talk to them.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI-WHYTE
utterances.text: I think the Trial Chamber will break here and we will resume at 2.30 for the afternoon session. (The Luncheon Adjournment). (2.30 pm).

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI-WHYTE
utterances.text: Good afternoon, ladies and gentlemen. So we continue from where we stopped.

utterances.speaker: MR. TURONE
utterances.text: Thank you, your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI-WHYTE
utterances.text: Inform the witness that he is still on his oath.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Mr. Kuljanin, may I remind you that you are still on your oath?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI-WHYTE
utterances.text: Carry on.

utterances.speaker: MR. TURONE
utterances.text: Thank you, your Honour. Mr. Kuljanin, during your stay in Celebici did you ever learn Mr. Landzo's first name?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, nor was I interested.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you used to call him with a nickname?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Going back to your arrest, Mr. Kuljanin, did anybody take your valuables on the occasion of your arrest?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What did they take from you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: They took a ring and a bracelet from me.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you ever get your property back?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: After your stay in Celebici, can you say when did you leave Celebici camp?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I can't say exactly -- I cannot say exactly, but I believe it was the November, beginning of December.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What happened to you when you left Celebici?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I was transferred to the Musala camp at Konjic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How long did you stay in the Musala camp?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Until the 3rd November 1993.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was that the day when you were released from any kind of detention?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes I alone was released from the Musala camp.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right, thank you very much, Mr. Kuljanin?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: You are welcome.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: This is the end of my examination-in-chief, your Honour, thank you very much?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI-WHYTE
utterances.text: Any cross-examination and the pattern in which you are agreed to take.

utterances.speaker: MR. O'SULLIVAN
utterances.text: Yes, we will proceeds this way first counsel for Mr. Delic, second counsel for Mr. Landzo, third counsel for Mr. Delalic and fourth counsel for Mr. Mucic

utterances.speaker: MR. MORAN
utterances.text: Your Honour, if I could have a second to get situated and plugged in. May it please the Court.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI-WHYTE
utterances.text: Yes, you can.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORAN
utterances.text: Thank you, your Honour. Good afternoon, sir.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Good afternoon.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORAN
utterances.text: My name is Tom Moran and I am a defence lawyer here and I am going to ask you some questions. Will you listen to the question that I ask and just answer that question. Can you do that for me, sir?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORAN
utterances.text: The other thing is, if you do not understand one of my questions, if I talk too fast or if my questions are hard to understand or you do not know what I am asking, will you stop me and ask me to repeat it?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORAN
utterances.text: Okay. So that you will not have any problems understanding the question. So there will not be any surprises, generally I am going it ask you questions pretty much in the order of the things that you were asked by Mr. Turone. So there will not be any surprises, but the first thing that I am going to ask you about is the last thing you talked about. You said you were released from Musala on November 3rd 1993, right?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORAN
utterances.text: That is not quite true, is it?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I did not say that I was released. I actually liberated myself from the camp and the torture that I was being subjected to. No one released me.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORAN
utterances.text: Yes, in fact you and several other people overpowered the guards and escaped, did you not?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, we did.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORAN
utterances.text: So if someone would have understood you to say that you were released, that would be a misunderstanding, would it not?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I was not released.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORAN
utterances.text: In fact when you overpowered that guards you took his weapon, did you not?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I did I took it.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORAN
utterances.text: You kidnapped him too, did you not?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, I did not, we did not. We let him go. We acted humanely towards him. We let him go home.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORAN
utterances.text: Where did you take him from the camp before you let him go home?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: He had truly led us. It was not us that led him. He was the one that had led us to the front line to dig trenches, but we took our chance, we disarmed him and we took him with us until we saw that we were safe. Then we let him go back to his home. We said goodbye to him in a humane fashion. We told him to tell the real truth about how we had treated him. Then we went on our way and crossed over to Croatian territory. The Croatian Army took us in. They were good to us. We spent a couple of hours. They gave us some food. Then they let us go on towards the Serbian territory.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORAN
utterances.text: Okay. Let us go back to the Battle of Bradina, if we could, okay. Can you do that for me? Did you have any weapons?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I personally did not have any.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORAN
utterances.text: None at all?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, none at all.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORAN
utterances.text: Not even a fully automatic 7.62 millimetres rifle?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORAN
utterances.text: The only weapons that were there in the whole city were a few pistols and hunting rifles. That is what you testified to under direct examination, all right?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: As far as I know, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORAN
utterances.text: You were pretty familiar with what was going on in Bradina, were you not?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: What was going on, I am sorry?

utterances.speaker: MR. MORAN
utterances.text: You were pretty well familiar with what kind of weapons people had in Bradina, were you not?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Sorry, I did not understand the question.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORAN
utterances.text: Sure. If people had weapons in Bradina, you pretty well knew about it. You had a pretty good idea about what various people had?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I knew some people who had personal weapons and I knew some who went hunting and had hunting weapons.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORAN
utterances.text: But you never saw any military-type weapons anywhere in the city; is that right?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORAN
utterances.text: So if they would have been around, you would have seen them, would you not?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Absolutely, I would have.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORAN
utterances.text: Your Honour, there is a series of photographs, I believe Delic exhibits, the weapons photographs, if those could be shown to the witness - just the ones that are in evidence. I am going to ask you to take a look at some pictures and see if there were any of these at all in Bradina, okay?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I can take a look at them.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORAN
utterances.text: By the way, before they come over there, you are familiar with military weapons because of your service in the military police; is that not right?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Absolutely.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORAN
utterances.text: That service in the military police --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I served with the Yugoslavia People's Army in 1987 and 1988 prior to the war - just to clarify.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORAN
utterances.text: I was going to get to that next. You served your two years of compulsory service in the Yugoslav National Army?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: One year.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORAN
utterances.text: You are being shown a group of pictures. If you go through those and see if you recollect any of those weapons as weapons you saw in Bradina before the Battle of Bradina?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, this one I saw when I was serving in the Yugoslav People Army. This one I've never seen.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORAN
utterances.text: Okay, that's fine. I believe there is some more pictures coming.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: This one I also saw while I was serving in the army.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORAN
utterances.text: But not in Bradina, prior to the Battle of Bradina?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORAN
utterances.text: How about that one?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That one I also saw while I was serving in the army and in movies, war movies that had been shown prior to the war, movies from the Second World War, that is.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORAN
utterances.text: But not in the Battle of Bradina?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORAN
utterances.text: That one?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I have, also while in the army.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORAN
utterances.text: But not in Bradina?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORAN
utterances.text: That one?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I have seen this one but not in Bradina.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORAN
utterances.text: Next. That is it. Okay. Were there any roadblocks put up by the people of Bradina to keep -- to keep people from going on the main road through the village?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, there were some blocks, but they were not erected by the villagers of Bradina, but by military formation Muslim and Croatian formation who blocked both tunnel through which one could pass through Bradina. I see no reason why anyone should erect any barricades after everything that had happened and why people should be stopped from passing through Bradina. I do not know of any such case, your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORAN
utterances.text: If somebody said somebody set up blocks through Bradina, those people would be lying or be wrong; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Absolutely.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORAN
utterances.text: There was absolutely no organised defence of Bradina, is that what you want the Court to understand your testimony to be?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes. If you say that there was some sort of an organised action mounted by soldiers in Bradina, there wouldn't be 80 dead people in Bradina killed by the unit which attacked it and numbers lost on their side. I believe that the victims tell all.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORAN
utterances.text: So I understand your answer; as I understand it, what you said was there was no organised defence of the village of Bradina. Is my understanding correct, sir?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, there was no organised defence and the victims are telling enough.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORAN
utterances.text: Okay, fine. Let us go on to your capture. You were captured either on 29th or 30th May 1992; is that right?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, somewhere around that time.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORAN
utterances.text: You were taken where, to a school, right?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, to a school in Ljuta, and from the school we were taken to Bjeljasinca to the Hotel Famos.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORAN
utterances.text: Let start with the school, you were kicked and beaten very severely at that school, were you not?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORAN
utterances.text: Then you were taken to the hotel?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORAN
utterances.text: Where you were beaten again, right?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORAN
utterances.text: And from the hotel you were put on a truck to head towards Celebici, right?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORAN
utterances.text: And it was cash --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: En route itself members of the Muslim paramilitary formations were escorting us on the truck shot at us, prisoners who were sitting on the floor of the truck and we were tied. On that occasion they killed a prisoner and wounded four of them.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORAN
utterances.text: I thought we had an agreement that you would listen to my questions and just answer the questions that I asked. If we do not have that agreement can we reach that agreement, sir?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Okay, absolutely, I am sorry.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORAN
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you. In fact Dragan Vudicic was shot on the way to the camp and several other people were wounded; is that not right?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORAN
utterances.text: Okay, when you arrived at Celebici -- let me back off just a second. You mentioned at the end of your direct examination that at some point after your arrest your property was taken from you; is that not right? Do you remember testifying to that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, my property was seized in tunnel number nine.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORAN
utterances.text: It was?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: In tunnel number nine.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORAN
utterances.text: Okay. Do you know a man called Zilic?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Zilic.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORAN
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORAN
utterances.text: Are you familiar with a building named -- and I am going to spell it, I cannot pronounce it, my Serbian is awfully poor -- D-R-U-S-T-V-E-N-I-D-O-M; are you familiar with that building, sir?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I am.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORAN
utterances.text: Where is that building?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It is in the centre of the city.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORAN
utterances.text: Okay, so do you remember making a statement to the office of the prosecutor over a two-day period in October 1995?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: What did I state -- I do not understand.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORAN
utterances.text: I am just asking you if you remember making a statement, sir?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Here at that building.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORAN
utterances.text: No, I am asking whether you remember making a statement to the office of the prosecutor in October 1995 after your escape?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I do not remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORAN
utterances.text: You do not remember making a statement at all?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORAN
utterances.text: If the usher could show him both an English and a Bosnian copy of this statement. So I am borrowing the English copy from Ms. McMurrey, so I have to have it back. Sir, if you look at the English version, because that is the original, does that look like your signature on it?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORAN
utterances.text: Now does that help you remember whether or not you made a statement to the office of the prosecutor?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORAN
utterances.text: In that statement, when you made that statement an investigator from the office of the prosecutor asked you some questions, right?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Right.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORAN
utterances.text: You would answer those questions and someone would write them down; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It is.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORAN
utterances.text: You knew that this was an important thing when you were making this statement; right?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORAN
utterances.text: You wanted to tell the truth in that statement, did you not?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORAN
utterances.text: In fact you told the truth and the whole truth and nothing but the truth when you made that statement; is that not right?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORAN
utterances.text: After you got through making the statement it was read back to you in Serbian; do you remember it now?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORAN
utterances.text: Then you had a chance to make any corrections that you wanted to make, did you not?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORAN
utterances.text: Any additions you wanted to make you could have added, right?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I could have, but I probably did not because I did not have enough time.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORAN
utterances.text: So the investigator from the office of the prosecutor rushed you so much that you did not have time to get the statement correct; is that what you are saying, sir?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, no, he did not rush me. I rushed my own self because I did not have time.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORAN
utterances.text: You were in a hurry, and because you were in a hurry you just rushed through this statement?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Umm hmm, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORAN
utterances.text: Because you were in a hurry to get about the rest of your business, right, whatever the rest of your business was?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I was also in a dilemma facing this honourable court here or not, so I did not pay that much attention to it.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORAN
utterances.text: So you were in so much of a hurry you did not pay so much attention to it; is that right?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Absolutely correct, I did not.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORAN
utterances.text: Did you read the "witness acknowledgment" on the page with your signature on it on the back? Why do you not take the Bosnian version right now and read it over, and I can read it in English and we can see if it says the same thing. It is way in the back where your signature it on the Bosnian version, approximately the last page. It says "witness acknowledgment". See if you can find that. Did you find it?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I found the witness acknowledgment.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORAN
utterances.text: Okay, let us go over it. Lets see what it says. I do not think that he has it. If someone could help him find it. It should be on the last page. Your Honour, we have another copy. We can let him read it off this. Sir, we are going to hand you another copy and we will take some copies back in a minute because you are getting loaded with paper, where it says "witness acknowledgment" up there at the top of the page?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORAN
utterances.text: On the page on the left-hand side.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, on the left side, but there is no signature.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORAN
utterances.text: I understand that, sir. That is a Bosnian translation from the original English. Let us go over this and see if this is what you read and had read to you. It says: "This statement has been read over to me in the Serbian language and is true to the best of my knowledge and recollection." Do you remember someone reading that sentence to you right before you signed? Do you remember that, sir? . Then they went on and said --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Not too well.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORAN
utterances.text: Then went on and said: "I have given this Statement voluntarily and am aware that it may be used in legal proceedings before the International Criminal Tribunal for the Prosecution of Persons Responsible for Serious Violations of International Law Committed in the Territory of the Former Yugoslavia since 1991, and that I may be called to give evidence ... before the Tribunal." Do you remember them saying that to you before you signed?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORAN
utterances.text: So it was made pretty clear to you, was it not, that this was and important interview and an important document, was it not?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORAN
utterances.text: This is an important criminal court since World War II, so that is a pretty big thing in your life?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORAN
utterances.text: But you were rushed when you gave the statement, so you are not sure whether you were correct or not; is that what you are telling the judges?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORAN
utterances.text: Let us go over some of the things in that statement. When you said, you said all your property was taken from you in tunnel nine. Now if you look at the Serbian statement, the translation, does it not say: "When we arrive at Konjic the convoy stopped in front of their military command, the building". The building's name was Drustveni Dom?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORAN
utterances.text: "Zilic ordered the soldiers in the truck to search us. Zilic ordered: 'Search them.' 'Take their ID cards and bring them to me.' The soldiers searched us, took all of our valuables and gave them to Zilic. "Zilic then said: 'I want everything. Don't let me catch you holding anything back from me'." You said that in your written statement, did you not?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, but there were some things that were hidden: for instance, they took my chain, but I also had a bracelet and a ring, as I already said, and I hid them. I gave those to them in tunnel number nine. They did not find it and I gave the gold chain to Zilic.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORAN
utterances.text: So when you said in your statement to the office of the prosecutors "The soldiers then searched us, took all our valuables and gave them to Zilic", that was incorrect; is that what you are saying? Pardon me, sir.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, they searched us, that is true, but they could not find everything because we hid it in our socks, in our shoes. Wherever somebody thought of that, they could put something away.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORAN
utterances.text: So they did not take all or valuables, just all the valuables that they could find, right?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I thought I would succeed to keep this ring. It was a present from my late mother and my bracelet; but I gave that up too in tunnel number nine.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORAN
utterances.text: Okay, now let us go on a little further in your testimony on direct. When you got to Celebici you were unloaded off the trucks, right?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORAN
utterances.text: Then you were lined up against a wall, was that before or after you were taken to the command building to be registered in into the camp?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I think it was after we were unloaded, as far as I can recall.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORAN
utterances.text: You mean after you were unloaded you were taken to the command building to be registered into the camp or after you were unloaded you were beaten and then taken into the command building to be registered into the camp. Which was it, sir?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It is difficult to remember all the details and all the facts with precision, because one has to bear in mind all the things that we went through before we got to Celebici, so that it was impossible to register and remember every single detail. It really is difficult, particularly now to recall every single detail.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORAN
utterances.text: I understand that it is hard to recall detail several years later. After this beating by people, you do not know who they were, that is what you testified to under direct, you do not know who beat you up when you got there?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: At first I did not know.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORAN
utterances.text: That beating was about three or four hours long. Then at some point you were put into tunnel nine; right?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORAN
utterances.text: You remained in tunnel nine for what, 110 or 120 days, which was if?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: About 110. Again, I am not quite sure whether it was 110 or 105, but something like that.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORAN
utterances.text: Okay, somewhere over 100 days?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORAN
utterances.text: You got there May 30th, June 1st, thereabouts?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, thereabouts.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORAN
utterances.text: In fact it could be either May 30th or June 1st, would it not?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORAN
utterances.text: There were no other prisoners in the tunnel when you were put into it; right?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: When we entered the tunnel was empty there were other prisoners who had been captured and brought to the camp, whether they had been in number nine before, I do not know, but it was empty when I entered the tunnel. There was no one there.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORAN
utterances.text: Okay. Eventually there were about 40 people in that tunnel; is that right?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: As far as I can remember, yes, maybe a little more or a little less, but that is roughly the number. I cannot give you the exact number.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORAN
utterances.text: Okay. You were only fed ever third day while you were in the tunnel, is that not right? Is that what you said in direct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, yes, we would get a slice of bread every third day, a slice of bread.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORAN
utterances.text: Not any more than that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORAN
utterances.text: If you take a look at your statement -- you can look at the Bosnian version -- I am going to read something and see if that is what you what your statement says. The paragraph starts off: "Because the tunnel was not long enough we did to sleep diagonally." See if you can find that in your statement, that paragraph.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It is not necessary, I do not have to look for it. I remember that.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORAN
utterances.text: Did you say in that written statement: "In the beginning, we received only a very small piece of bread and half a cup of water once a day"?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I may have said that, but the truth is we got a slice of bread every third day.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORAN
utterances.text: What you put in your statement to the office of the prosecutor, it was not the truth, is that what you are saying?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Maybe I was wrong; I made a mistake. I cannot recall now. Maybe I was not concentrating enough at the time I was making this statement. I already said that I was in a hurry. Maybe I made some omissions as a result of that.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORAN
utterances.text: Okay. One thing I do need to clear up: . there was a guard named Osman Dedic, right?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORAN
utterances.text: He is different from Hazim Delic, right?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Osman Dedic.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORAN
utterances.text: Yes. He and Hazim Delic are two different people; right?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORAN
utterances.text: Now in your direct examination you testified -- I am looking for it in my notes -- that you were beaten three or four times personally. Do you remember testifying to that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORAN
utterances.text: You also testified that every time you went out to use the latrine you were lined up against the wall and beaten with a baseball bat; do you remember testifying to that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, yes, that is what I said, but we did not understand one another well. That was when I was beaten on my own as an individual, but we went to the latrine in a group. So I was singling out the occasions when I was singled out to be beaten. But when I was beaten as a member of a group, that happened almost daily.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORAN
utterances.text: Okay. Let us talk about these baseball bat beatings for a minute; okay? When you say Mr. Delic hit you with a baseball bat, he, what, hit you across the back, did he not?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORAN
utterances.text: He hit you real hard, did he not?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORAN
utterances.text: About how many times would he hit you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It depended, sometimes more, sometimes less. I did not count. I could not count.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORAN
utterances.text: Would it be fair to say he hit you more than 10 times with that baseball bat?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I cannot recall.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORAN
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Because it depended on the strength of the blow and it depended on pain. So for us one blow could be equal 100 sometimes and sometimes less.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORAN
utterances.text: Well, okay, you told me he was hitting you real hard every time he hit you. Did I misunderstand you on that, sir?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: If he had intended not to hit me hard he probably would not have hit me at all. I am sure he did not want to caress me.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORAN
utterances.text: So he was hitting you about as hard as he could?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Whether he could hit harder, I really don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORAN
utterances.text: He hit you across the kidneys, is that not what you said?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORAN
utterances.text: In fact if you were going to be hit with a baseball bat you would be hit across the kidneys with that baseball bat; right?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It depended on the will of the person hitting you.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORAN
utterances.text: Okay. So you were not always hit across the kidneys. Do you know where your kidneys are by the way, so that we understand each other?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I should know, surely.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORAN
utterances.text: They are in the lower part of your back, one on each side.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORAN
utterances.text: Below your rib cage; right?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORAN
utterances.text: So that they are not protected by any bones from sharp blows; right?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: As you know yourself.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORAN
utterances.text: Yes, I just wanted to make sure that we were on the same wave length. If the usher could show you --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORAN
utterances.text: -- the baseball bat.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I can see it; I am familiar with it. You do not need to show it to me.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORAN
utterances.text: That looks like the baseball bat that was used; right?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORAN
utterances.text: It was used to hit you real hard?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORAN
utterances.text: It was used to --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Would you please remove it from the table, please? Can I ask for that?

utterances.speaker: MR. MORAN
utterances.text: Sure, no problem. Sure. That looks like the baseball bat that you say Mr. Delic swung inside the tunnel to hit people with; right?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORAN
utterances.text: Did you testify the tunnel was about 1.2 metres wide; right?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: According to my estimate. I did not measure it.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORAN
utterances.text: Give or take a little bit, maybe a little more or maybe a little less?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, roughly. I really do not know exactly how wide it was.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORAN
utterances.text: Let us go to the incidents about the manhole. Let us talk about that for a second.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORAN
utterances.text: That is a pretty memorable experience, is it not?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORAN
utterances.text: Not the kind of thing that somebody would forget, is it?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORAN
utterances.text: Sir, take the Serbian version of your statement and read out loud the entire way you recounted that to the office of the prosecutor?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I do not know if I can find it.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORAN
utterances.text: Sir, I will help you: you will not find it because it is not there. About how big was the bottom of that manhole in square metres?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It was very small. I know how we felt inside and how much space we had. We know that very well how small it was.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORAN
utterances.text: At the time you were all put in that manhole, there were, what, about 40 people in the tunnel?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I said that I really do not know the exact number, 30 to 40 people. I cannot recall that. I have already said that, that I do not know the exact number.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORAN
utterances.text: Well, you gave a list of 41 names in your statement. Would that be right?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I did provide a list.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORAN
utterances.text: There were 41 names on that list, were not there?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, but people left tunnel number nine before others and some did not go to the manhole at all. A couple of people who were from the same locality as the camp was.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORAN
utterances.text: Sir, maybe I misunderstood your direct examination -- I am going through my notes -- I thought you said that they took a group of about 16 or 17 and that you were in that group, and after that they let you out of the tunnel they took everybody else and put them down in the manhole?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, but as far as I can remember a couple of people did not go to the manhole. I am not sure about that. I think those people who came from the same place as the camp itself, so I am not quite sure about that.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORAN
utterances.text: Okay, so you are not sure. You were not sure when you testified on direct that after your group was put back in tunnel nine everybody else in tunnel nine got put in the manhole?

utterances.speaker: MR. TURONE
utterances.text: Okay, your Honour. He did not actually say "everybody else" but talked about a second group.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORAN
utterances.text: Your Honours have heard the testimony. I am just going off my memory. Its's in the transcript whatever he said.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORAN
utterances.text: Slavko Susic, let's talk about his death.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORAN
utterances.text: And Zara Mrkajic's connection with that death, okay?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I do not understand. There was no Zara. Zara was not in tunnel number nine. Mrkajic?

utterances.speaker: MR. MORAN
utterances.text: Zara Mrkajic.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, Zara was there, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORAN
utterances.text: Are you familiar with a thing called the Republika Sirpska?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I am.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORAN
utterances.text: Tell the judges what Republika Sirpska is?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: A territory under the control of Serbs, the territory that belonged to the Serbs.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORAN
utterances.text: In fact it has a government, army and a court system; right?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Probably. I am not following the news.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORAN
utterances.text: Well, I am just curious whether or not you knew that Zoran Mrkajic spent eight months in the custody of the Republika Sirpska while they investigated his connection with Mr. Susic's death. I am curious whether you knew Grozda Cecez was one of the main prosecution witnesses against you, did you know that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, I have no idea about that.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORAN
utterances.text: Okay, that is fine. Let us talk about the Red Cross now for a minute; okay?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORAN
utterances.text: When the Red Cross came on their very first visit to register everybody where you in hangar six or tunnel nine?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: In tunnel number nine.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORAN
utterances.text: Okay. Let us talk a little bit about your interrogations. On direct examination, frankly it was not clear to me -- and I am not criticising anyone -- it just was not clear to me, you said that there were two people who interrogate you. In the same sentence you said "and who escorted us to the office and stood as security while we were being interrogated." Did you mean there were two people interrogating you and two people who escorted you to and from the office?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I was thinking of the guards who accompanied us. Of course there were another two interrogating us. I do not know their names. Nor do I know the names of those who escorted us to the Command building.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORAN
utterances.text: What I am getting at is it is two groups of two people?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Two people interrogated us and two people brought me to the Command building and they were waiting like security until I made some sort of a statement.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORAN
utterances.text: Okay. About how long after you were brought to the camp did this interrogation occur - one week, two weeks?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I cannot remember. I do not remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORAN
utterances.text: You do not recall. Do you recall whether it was a short time or a long time?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: After a short time. I think it was at the beginning. I cannot remember exactly how -- after how many days. That I cannot remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORAN
utterances.text: But it was definitely after June 1st; no question about that, right?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I think not.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORAN
utterances.text: If you arrived at the camp about June 1st you were not interrogated the first day you were there, were you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I do not remember because I was in a poor condition. Maybe some people were interrogated, maybe I was too, but I do not remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORAN
utterances.text: That is fair enough, you were in a poor condition because of the beating you took at Mount Igman and at the school and on your way to Celebici; right?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORAN
utterances.text: Did you have any medical treatment for your injuries?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, never.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORAN
utterances.text: How about after you left the camp?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Me? I did in Republika Sirpska or, rather, in Serbian, when I left the camp.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORAN
utterances.text: Do you have copies of those medical records?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORAN
utterances.text: I noticed that you testified on direct that at the time of the Battle of Bradina you were not a member of the Serbian Democratic Party, "but I have since become a member of the Serbian Democratic Party"; is that not what you testified to?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORAN
utterances.text: You now support the SDS and its leaders?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Whether I support them or not, that is my own affair. Whether I support anyone, whether I support the SDS at all, that is my personal affair, and my own option, I suppose. I am entitled to that.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORAN
utterances.text: That is true: where I come from some of us are Democrats and some of us are Republicans and we can pretty much be what we want to be. Let me jump back a second. Do you recall in March 1992 there was a plebisite, an election in Bosnia Herzegovina?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I know that there were some kind of elections.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORAN
utterances.text: I am not going to ask you whether you voted in it or how you voted, if you did vote; the only thing I want to know is, if you wanted to vote, if you had the desire to go vote in that election, could you have done that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I do not know. I cannot tell.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORAN
utterances.text: Well, were you on the Voter Registration Rolls for Bradina?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I do not know that either.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORAN
utterances.text: Were you on the voter registration?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I was without an ID card for a long time. I was not registered in Bradina even.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORAN
utterances.text: You were without an ID cards for a long time. When did you lose your ID cards, sir, roughly?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I lost it some time before the war. I cannot recall exactly how long before.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORAN
utterances.text: Okay. So because you did not have an ID card you were ineligible to vote, is that it?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I probably could not have voted without an ID card, without some kind of documents.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORAN
utterances.text: Just one more thing -- and I may have asked it poorly a little bit earlier, but if I have I apologise -- I just want to make sure we have it clear, then I think we will be pretty much close to done. It is your position based on having been in Bradina prior to the Battle of Bradina that these people, the residents of Bradina -- okay -- did not have any kind of military force there, no partisans, no regular army, no militia, no organisation at all. That is what you are testifying to; right?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, that is what I said. In answer to the gentleman's question I said "No".

utterances.speaker: MR. MORAN
utterances.text: So there was not anybody there that was a commander or there was not anybody there that was wearing some kind of insignia to show that they were in a military unit, on the Serb side; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I do not know whether there was a single prisoner who came to the camp in a uniform, except for -- all of them had civilian clothes and sneakers. If that is army, people under arms, I am not familiar that any such case exists in the world.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORAN
utterances.text: I agree with you wholeheartedly, sir. Are you familiar with a man named Radovan Karadzic?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORAN
utterances.text: What is his relationship to the Serbian Democratic Party?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I have no idea.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORAN
utterances.text: I pass the witness, your Honour

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI-WHYTE
utterances.text: Mr. Ackerman, you can proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: Thank you very much, your Honour. Mr. Kuljanin, my name is John Ackerman. I represent Mr. Landzo in this Court. How are you this afternoon.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, please, Mr. Ackerman.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: Did you hear what I said?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: When you first came into this Court this morning to testify you stood and took an oath to tell the truth, did you not?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: Have you ever done that before anywhere else? Have you ever taken an oath anywhere else to tell the truth?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Not on occasions like these, no, I have not been in a situation to take an oath to tell the truth. I have not had occasion to be on the witness stand so far.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: So this is your first experience as a witness being asked questions and giving answers to those questions in this kind of a setting; is that a fair statement?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: Now, you do have some experience with being asked questions in a less formal setting about your experiences during the situation that arose in Bosnia in 1992, do you not?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I really did not understand the question.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: Well, you have been asked questions by a representative of the office of the prosecutor. You have been asked questions by military investigating committees and Celebici and perhaps in Konjic before about the event in Bosnia in 1992, have you not?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, I do not remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: I thought we had at least established when Mr. Moran was up here that you now have a memory of being questioned by Mr. Hortemo from the office of the prosecutor?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: You are referring to the International Tribunal, when I gave statements for the Tribunal? Is this what you are referring to?

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: I am referring to every time somebody has sat you down and asked you questions about your experience in Bosnia in 1992. That has happened before, has not it?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: Now you have had a chance to look at the statement you gave to the office of the prosecutor for this Tribunal in October 1995, have you not?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: When was the last time you saw that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I cannot recall, really.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: You never saw that since you have arrived here at the Hague until Mr. Moran showed it to you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, I did not.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: No one from the office of the prosecutor --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I do not remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: -- no one from the office of the prosecutor in talking to you about the testimony you were going to give here today showed you that statement and gave you an opportunity to read it?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, they gave me something, but I did not read anything. I was not very interested in those statements.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: You mean just in the last few days here in The Hague you were given something to read by the prosecutor to read but chose not to because you were not very interested?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: Are you interested in being here at all today?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I am interested in recounting my experiences and what I felt under my own skin. I have not come here to lie nor waste my time before this honourable Court. I should like to thank the honourable Court to give me this opportunity to say what I have to say and to say what I have gone through. I am not interested in statements. I want to tell before the Court what I have gone through and what I have felt in my own skin, the statements that can be read by whoever sees fit and who needs them.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: In fact when you came into this court the first thing this morning and were sworn, the first thing you said was to the Court "May I begin?" like you were prepared to go ahead and make a statement without any questions being asked of you at all; correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, no, I did not say that. I actually waited for someone to put a question because I had no idea. I also had some stage fright because standing before this eminent honourable Court I did not feel all that pleasant and I was struck with stage fright as well. I only started talking after questions had been asked of me.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: Did you have any idea that Mr. Turone was going to ask you questions today?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: You had no conversation prior to coming here with Mr. Turone where he told you that he was going to be asking you questions?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: Did you have any conversation with --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I am not quite sure what gentleman you are referring to. The gentleman who just asked me some questions before?

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: Yes, the one right there who keeps raising his hand. If you look over, he will raise his hand so that you can see. That gentleman.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Oh, yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: Yes. What --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Well, he talked to me about how I should behave, that I should tell the truth and so on.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: Is he the one that gave you your statement to look at that you decided not to look at?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, he gave me some papers, but I chose not to look at any papers because I really know what my own experience is which I came to tell the honourable Court about.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: Did you know what your experiences had been in October 1995 when you talked to Mr. Hortemo or were you having a blackout of some kind that day?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I probably could not remember some things then, and subsequently I supplemented some of the things I said because I had forgotten them before.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: So your memory is better now than it was a couple of years ago?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It is not a question of that. As far as the camp itself is concerned, I could write novels. One could write novels about it and just say something within a limited space of time because one remembers things that one has forgotten before and did not recall at a certain point of time.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: Well, Mr. Moran just asked you a question about your interrogation when you got to Celebici and you told the Court that it is very difficult to remember the details of what happened because it is so long ago. Now, you are telling us you have no problem remembering all the details because it is so clear in your mind. Which one of those is it?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Of course I cannot remember all the details. I did not tell the gentleman all the details. I cannot, it is impossible for one to recall all the details because there were so many things.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: If you had had an opportunity while you were in Celebici camp to keep a diary of those experiences, that could be real helpful to you today to help refresh your memory to be more accurate, would it not?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, it would. I have no opportunity to think about my own life. I only waited for the day that I would leave, so I had no opportunity nor the time to think about keeping any records. I had no sense of the time. I did not know what day it was, what month it was, let alone keep any records. It was impossible.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: Please understand, I am not suggesting that you should have kept a diary. The other thing I would like to ask is that you listen carefully to my questions - you tend to make little speeches at the end of my questions. If my question is not real clear to you, let me know and I will try to make it more clear. But if you will do that, we will get out of here a lot quicker today; okay?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: How should I know how exactly to answer? . I answer the way exactly I think I should answer.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: That is okay so long as your answer has something to do with the question that I asked; okay?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: Now having told us that if you had kept a diary while at Celebici it would have been helpful in terms of refreshing your memory about what happened there; I take it the same would be true if you had made statements about the time you were in Celebici or thereafter. It would certainly be helpful to review those just to see if there was something there that you might not remember today that you would like to tell this Tribunal about?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I have already said that I maintain no lists, no records of any kind. I do not know. I do not understand.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: The officers of the prosecutor made a record of your account of what happened to you there. That record was made in October 1995 in the form of a statement that you gave to the office of the prosecutor. Now you know that is true, do you not?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: That statement was made over a period of two days. It was made during the 20th and 21st October 1995; are you aware of that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: You understood that that statement was being taken by a representative of this Tribunal of the office of the prosecutor of this Tribunal and that that was an important matter, did you not?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I have no idea how important it is.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: Well, I guess you think it is important enough that you are here today?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: What is important is for me to tell this honourable Court about the things that I have gone through.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: And in October 1995 it was important for you to tell a representative of the office of the prosecutor and this honourable Court what you had gone through; correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, but not as much as here today, because I was in a dilemma whether to appear before the Tribunal or not.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: So I guess you told Mr. Hortemo that there were a lot of things that you just were not going to tell him on those two days, that you spoke with limit because you were having this dilemma. Did you tell him that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I did. I said that I would only be making a brief statement because at that time I did not believe that I would be appearing before the Tribunal. So I just gave him a brief description of what did happen.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: So over a period of two days you gave him a brief statement?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The time was limited by me. My time was limited. I only had so much time that I could allot to that.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: You met with him on two different days, on 20th and 21st October; did not you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, we met on those two days.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: Do you think Mr. Hortemo would agree with you that you were only going to give him part of the story?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I did not say to him that I would give him a part of the story. I only said that my time was limited and that I did not have enough time because I had some business to attend to and I gave him the statement which I did. If I did give a statement, it does not mean that I said everything, that it is exhaustive.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: So you did not did not tell Mr. Hortemo, as, you indicated earlier, that you were only going to tell him part of the story. Is that your testimony now?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, I did not say that.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: Did you tell him that you were going to tell him everything that you could remember?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I said that I would tell him everything that I could remember then. At the moment in question that is what I gave him a statement of the thing that I could remember at the moment in question. As I was not concentrating enough, I was not ready, really ready to make a statement, I said what I said.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: He told you that it was real important that you tell him everything you could remember, did he not?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, he did. He told me so.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: He told you at that time that he was there to take your statement because Mr. Delalic and Mr. Delic and Mr. Landzo and Mr. Mucic had been indicted by this Tribunal and he wanted to know if you had any information about any of those people as a result of your experience. He told you that, did he not?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, he did.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: Now a few moments ago when Mr. Turone, the prosecutor, who asked you questions, was questioning you, he asked you if you had any opportunity to learn Mr. Landzo's first name or nickname and you told him, "No" that you did not have that opportunity. Is that not what you said?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
