utterances.text: I said that I knew him by his nickname and that I knew his surname. For his name I was not really interested. If I had wanted to know I would have found out in the camp itself.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: Well, you told --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: As far as his first name is concerned.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: You told Mr. Hortemo when you talked to him that his name was Senad Landzo. That the person who tortured you was Senad Landzo?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I said that I thought the first name was Senad. I was not sure. I was sure about his surname and his nickname. I wasn't sure about his first name and that is exactly what I said.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: Why do you think Mr. Hortemo failed to record you 'thought' that was his name and just put it down as you 'said' that was his name. Why would he have done that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I really have no idea. I do not know, maybe that is his name.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: Why, when you had a chance to review this statement and it was read to you, why did you not say. 'Wait a minute, I am not sure that is the name'?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It just did not occur to me. I was not interested very much in that person, whether the name is this or that. I know who they are and what they are, and as far as I am concerned that is sufficient.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: So your position here today is that, as far as you know, the person named Landzo who did the things that you have described was a person named Senad Landzo; correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I repeat, I am not sure about the name, the first name. I am sure about the surname and his face and his physical appearance, that I am sure of. As far as the first, I am not sure whether it is this or that. I am quite sure about his physical appearance, his surname and his nickname.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: A few moments ago when I was asking you about the statement that you gave to the office of the prosecutor, Mr. Hortemo, you responded in a way to make that plural, like you had given more than one statement to the office of the prosecutor. Have you given them more than one statement?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I don't -- I cannot recall. I have no idea.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: You do not remember whether you met with a representative of the office of the prosecutor other than on 20th and 21st October?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It seems to me that some people did come after that date also, but I was not really interested. I do not know.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: Do you remember giving any other statements to anyone regarding the event in and around Bradina in 1992?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I do not remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: You certainly remember giving a statement to the military investigating committee at Celebici when you were taken into the Command centre there. You have described that and you gave a statement there, did you not?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I did. I gave some statements, as I have already said.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: And that statement was given on June 8th 1992, the one at Celebici, was it not?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It might have been.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: And in that statement you told the members of that Committee that you had been a member of the SDS since the SDS was formed, did you not?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That is what is written there. Whether I said it is a question, I know for a fact I did not say that I was a member of the SDS. I said that I was not. The fact is that I was not a member and they wrote that I was. He cursed my Chetnik mother and he said we were all the same and that we were all members. I do not know what else they wrote there, but this is the way it was.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: You told that Committee that you knew there was four mortars located in the village of Bradina. One mortar of 82 millimetres was placed in the village of Barakusa. Damjan Gligorevic was an aiming gunner, while Goran Gligorevic was his assistant. The other mortar of 82 millimetres was placed at the Bara place above the house of Mrkajics and was operated by Zoran Kuljanin as an aiming gunner and Zeljko Makajic as his assistant the anti-aircraft mortar was placed at the Podgaj place above the house of Mrkajics, and I know that Zdravko Dordic, Zoran Dordic and Dragan Dordic were responsible for it. The radio station PCR-320 was placed next to the meteorological station at Bradina. , you told them all that, did you not?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Its people who are referred to in here, there, are people I do not even know. I never said these things nor did I see any of those things.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: How do you know what is in this statement, this statement of June 8th, 1992? How do you know what it says?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: You just read out parts of it to me.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: I started reading out the part about you being a member of the SDS party. You said: "They put that in there, but I did not say that." How do you know they said that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Sorry?

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: How do you know they put in there, that you were a member of the SDS party? You just told us they put it in there and it was not true; how do you know that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I know they asked me about it and I know what they put in after they asked me. They probably put it in there which does not mean anything to me.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: During the round-up in Bradina, you were a squadron commander, were you not?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Me? No. No, I was not.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: In your squad were people named Relja Gligorevic, Stevan Kuljanin, Nedo Kuljanin, Slavko Miljanic, Jelenko Kuljanin, Mitar Kuljanin, Milan Draganic. Those were the men in your squad, were they not?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No. I do not know two of the people you enumerated. I do not know them at all. I was not a squadron commander nor was I in charge of any people, of any men.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: After you left Bradina trying to escape in a canyon up near Ljuta, you ran into a member of the territorial defence and captured him, did you not?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: Disarm him?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: And later you captured an additional two members of the territorial defence and disarmed both of them; correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I was not in this group which disarmed the next two men because we had parted and this man who was armed with this rifle went with us escorting us to show us the way towards Serb controlled territory. I was not in that other group, and the other group captured the other two people that you are referring to.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: Were you in the group at that that Zara Mrkajic talked into surrendering because you were surounded?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Zara Mrkajic remained behind my group and he came to the village. He was not with me when we were captured. He was not there at all. He stayed behind and he went to the village and he was captured in Ljuta and disarmed, etc.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: Do you know a gentleman by the name of Vukasin Mrkajic?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: That is the person who was responsible forearming the citizens of Bradina, was it not?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I really have know idea what his function was and what he had. I really do not know.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: Did he not at one point give you an anti-aircraft gun and 80 bullets?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, not to me.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: Then later did you not exchange that with Mr. Dragan Vujicic for a 762 millimetres weapon?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: To make things clear I never exchanged anything of the kind, nor did I get any kind of armaments from Vukasin Mrkajic.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: So if you said all that in a statement that you signed, those things were not true?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: First of all, there is another Milenko in Bradina and he has the same surname. Perhaps some things might have been confused, because of that he has the same surname and the same name, possibly another man is involved.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: Is your father Stevan?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, he is.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: Is your mother Bosiljka?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, she was Bosiljka.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: So if this statement refers to a Milenko Kuljanin, son of Stevan and Bosiljka Kuljanin, that would be you, would it not?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: You have proper information but can I ask you a question, sir?

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: Go ahead. I'll let you do that.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: You have the data, particulars of my parents, can I ask you whether you have any details about who killed my mother in the village of Bradina, whether you have it in any of your documents which are so extensive and so full? Perhaps it is written who killed my mother in one of those.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: I don't, but you might ask Mr. Turone that. The prosecutors have a lot more documents than we do.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI-WHYTE
utterances.text: We will now see the dangers of getting into the dialogue.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: I was trying to be a good guy and let him ask me a question, and that was a mistake.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I apologise.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: That is all right. That was my fault. I would like to ask the usher to just show you the statement that I have been referring to and maybe get it marked and just have you let me know if that is your signature that is on that statement. (Handed)

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: Okay. Your Honour, I am getting ready to go into a second statement now, do you want to take the break now?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI-WHYTE
utterances.text: Yes, we will come back at 4.30. The Trial Chamber will resume at 4.30. (Short adjournment). (4.30 pm)

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI-WHYTE
utterances.text: Yes, you may proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: Thank you very much your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI-WHYTE
utterances.text: Remind him he is still on his oath.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Mr. Kuljanin, may I remind you that you are still under oath?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: Your Honour, with the assistance of the usher, I will ask that another statement be shown to this witness and see if he can identify this one.

utterances.speaker: MR. TURONE
utterances.text: May I ask to see this second statement?

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: It is my understanding that both of these were furnished to the office of the prosecutor months ago. Of course I was not here months ago.

utterances.speaker: MR. TURONE
utterances.text: No, there was not given to the prosecution, so we would like please to serve it in English translation, too, please, if it is possible up.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: Let me give this to Mr. Turone (Handed). Mr. Kuljanin, you have been handed a statement in Serbo-Croatian, I believe. I would like the registry to tell us how it is marked.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Registrar D16/4.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: D16/4, do you recognise that document?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: That is your signature that appears at the end of that; correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: That is a statement that you gave to the Military Investigating Commission of the Fourth Corps on January 11th, 1993; is it not?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That was when I just went there to sign a document. I was not aware of what kind of statement was at stake.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: Well, if you look at the last sentence in that statement, it says: "I gave the statement voluntarily and I accept and sign it as such." Is that not what it says there?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I already said that we went there just to sign the statement and I only now see what it is that I signed.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: Well, your signature to that statement, among other things, was an agreement that you accepted it and signed it voluntarily. Then it was witnessed by five people, was it not?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The truth is that I just signed it. I do not know how many witnesses there were, nor whether there were any witnesses. I put that signature in SUP in Musala. It was not just me. There were several of us and I now see what I have signed.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: Is this the first time you have seen it since the day that you signed it?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It is the first time I see this statement.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: There are a number of things in it that you would concede are absolutely true are not there?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I did not see it, so I do not know what it says. I do not know what part of it I can confirm and what not.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: Well, you can certainly confirm that during your attempted escape from Bradina you came across a TO member armed with a rifle. You disarmed him and he agreed to show you the way to Kalinovik. You would agree with that, would you not?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, he happened to come across us. He suddenly found himself amidst us and he did not really have time to use his rifle. So, it was just carelessness. We had no problems with him, nor did he have any problems with us. We just asked the boy to lead us to the way to Kalinovik.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: But you wound up disarming him? You took his weapon. Somebody in your group took his weapon?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, somebody did take his rifle from him.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: And he failed to survive that experience also, did he not?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: What do you mean, he did not survive.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: He was killed, was he not?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, no, that is not true that he was killed.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: Is it not also true that, during your escape, this guard that you kidnapped and used in the escape that you told us in a very humanitarian way that you let go and let go home was also killed, not let go home, by you guys, did not you guys kill him too?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That is not true. That is not correct. There is evidence. There are doctors who established the cause of his death and the place of his death, and as for us we treated him in a very humanitarian manner, if we are talking about the guards when we escaped from the camp.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: Did you kill anyone else during the process of that escape?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, my group, the group I was in at Ljuta did not. As for the other group that split from us, I am not sure. I was not there, so I cannot say. They may have. I cannot confirm that.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: There is no question about whether that guard that was with you during your escape wound up dead. You agree with that; correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That is what I heard. They found him, a commission came on the spot. The doctors came. They established the cause of death. He was not killed. He was not tortured. We treated him like human beings and he treated us correctly.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: Now in this statement you say that Rajko Djordjic came to Bradina in March 1992 and took command of the village; correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I have no idea about Rajko Djordjic, nor do I know the man well. I just know him by sight. He was working in Konjic. I was in Bradina, so that I do not know much about Rajko or when he came from Konjic. I just knew through a relative of his that he was working in a company in Konjic. I do not even know which. So I cannot say much about him.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: Mr. Kuljanin, I am not asking you that question. That was an interesting answer, but I want you to look at the statement. You have got it there, please look at it. My question is, does it not say there that in March 1992 Rajko Djordjic came to Bradina and immediately took command in the village, yes or no, does it say that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It does, as you say, but I already said that I signed a document without knowing what was in it.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: I understand that you want to sit here and deny the truth of the things that are in the statement that you signed, but I am going to insist on asking you the questions as to what is in that statement and insist you tell me whether it is there or not. Can you tell me?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: Okay. That statement also says there were four mortars located in Bradina, does it not?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: That statement also said that there was a radio transmitter RC-320 near the meteorological station, does it not?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Whatever you ... I do not know.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: It is in front of you. Please look at it.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I have already said that I signed a document without knowing what was in it. I can read the document and then tell you what it says, but whatever it says there, I really do not know Rajko Djordjic nor do I remember any radio station nor what position Rajko Djordjic had.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: It says in the statement, does it not, that you were a squad leader and names the people what were in your squad, does it not?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I heard that from the defence and I have already said that I was not a squad leader and that I do not even know some of the names that you read out, that are mentioned in this list and whose commanders I allegedly was.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: Do you understand that I am just asking you what the statement says. I am only asking, does it not say that in the statement? . I wanted to confirm that is what it says in the statement. Now the answer to that question must be yes, that it says that you were a squad leader and names some people. That is true. It says that in the statement, does it not?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, it says that in the statement, but I was not a leader of those men, nor do I know some of the names or some of the people whose names are on that list.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: Now, I want to go back for a moment to the statement that you gave to Mr. Hortemo of the office of the prosecutor in October 1995. If for some reason today you decided you wanted to deny the contents of that statement, you could simply say to this Tribunal 'I did not get a chance to read it. I have no idea what the in it.' You could say that about this statement too, could not you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, no. I can only say what I know. I cannot say I was a commander and that I led some people that I did not lead and some of which I did not even know. How can I confirm that? How can I say that?

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: According to this piece of paper that you have there in front of you, that is what you told five members of the Military Investigating Commission on January 11th 1993. That is what this paper indicates, does it not?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, yes, that is what it says in the paper, but the circumstances were such that one had to sign whatever was put on the table. You just had to sign it. It was not a normal prison. It was not a normal investigation. It was a camp, a concentration camp in which people were tortured and killed. When one brother hit another brother and did all kind of other things that I would rather not talk about.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: But on January 11th, 1993, you were not at Celebici, you had already left there; right?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, but I was in the Musala camp. It was not a hotel; that too was a camp.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: So the position you want to take here today is that in both of these statements that I have shown you, the one from Celebici camp, the one from Musala, that the things you said there were not true, largely?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I did not make this such statements, especially for this latter one. I do not remember stating anything. I just know we went to the military command in SUP to sign some documents and at certain point we were even told we were signing discharge papers and that we would be released.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: Either of these statements, at least on the face of them, indicated that you signed them voluntarily and that you -- that they were true to the best of your knowledge. Both of those statements that we have been talking about here for the last few minutes, say that do you they not?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I was not in a position to quarrel with them or to have a fight with them. Of course it had to be voluntary. How else do you think?

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: The same is true of the statement that you gave to the office of the prosecutor. You signed a statement at the end of that acknowledging that it was voluntary and true to the best of your knowledge?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: You are talking about the prosecution of the Tribunal.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: Yes?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: And for this --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Something different.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: And for this Tribunal to try to figure out which of these statements you were telling the truth in, the only thing we have is your word saying 'I did not mean that one but I meant that one'; correct?

utterances.speaker: MR. TURONE
utterances.text: Objection, your Honour. Asked and answered several times by the witness. He explained how come he had to sign the two statements in 1992 and 1993. He explained something quite different about the statement given to the office of the prosecution.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: Well, your Honour, I can just respond to that that just before we left here for a fortnight break, the prosecutor put on a witness from the Commission saying that these people were not forced to make statements. The statements were given absolutely voluntarily and so there is a conflict between the witness they put on two weeks ago and this one, apparently as to whether these statement are voluntary or not. I will leave that up to the Court do wrestle with.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI-WHYTE
utterances.text: Thank you very much. I would say the same thing, because if we are equating it to the Commission, the Commission and the prosecutors, the investigating officers might think otherwise.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: I want to go to something else now.

utterances.speaker: MR. TURONE
utterances.text: Your Honour, may I ask, please, that the two statements of 1992 and 1993 be admitted in evidence because the fact that they are in many parts almost identical, even in the wording, supports the witness's testimony of today that the statement were written by others and only signed by him.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: Your Honour, I totally agree with that. I want them admitted and I was going to do that later on in this process. I do not think we have an English version of that marked yet, and that probably should be done, but the two Serbo-Croatian versions I know are marked.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI-WHYTE
utterances.text: : The application appears to be unanimous, the defence and the prosecution.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: Now, the part of that that I don't accept is Mr. Turone's testimony that he made in terms of his offer. That is for the Court to decide and not for him to give testimony about. Here is an English version of that one and they are admitted, I guess, is that correct, your Honour?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI-WHYTE
utterances.text: Well, they are.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: The first statement will be D 15/4 and D16/4. I would need a translation of the first statement.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JAN
utterances.text: Can I have the statement?

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: That is the one I just handed you. Here are three more that we can give to the judges. This is the first one. You should have already the translation of the second one, do you not, or did we just give that to the prosecution?

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: You just gave it to the prosecution.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: I have one marked up. Here we go. All right. Are you familiar with a gentleman by the name of Desimir Mrkajic?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: Mr. Mrkajic was in that group of you who escaped from Bradina in May 1992 during the attack on Bradina; correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: Is Bradina a very, very big city?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It is not a city; it's a village, a rather large village.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: Is it a village that is so large that people on one side of town have no idea what is going on on the other side of town?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, because it is scattered; it is a large village.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: So someone who was there could say that everybody in Bradina was armed and defended the city and somebody else there could say nobody there was armed and we did not defend the city, and those would not be inconsistent statements, because it is so big; is that true?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I apologise. I did not understand you at all. I thought you were not asking me anything.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: I am asking you this. One of the dilemmas that I have is between the testimony you gave here today, for instance, that to your knowledge nobody in Bradina was armed, and other witnesses that we have heard here from Bradina who said basically everybody there was armed. I am just curious as to how two different people could have two different views of that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: But how is it possible for somebody who lived in Bradina, and there were no Muslims, it was virtually a pure Serb village, to force somebody to tell newspaper reporters that he had raped Muslim women and tortured Muslim children? Why is that possible? It is not possible at the same time for somebody to say that there were military formation. There were tanks. There were planes, and who knows what else and besides which they beat us and killed us.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: I am not talking about that; I am talking about someone who was a Serbian resident of Bradina who has been here as a witness, someone who you probably know. What I do not understand is how --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I am not interested what other people said. I am not interested in other people's statements. I came here to make a statement of my own and to tell the honourable Court the truth, to tell them what I know and what I lived through and what some other people said. To whom they said it, when they said it, I am simply not interested.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: Do you think Desimir Mrkajic "who I know" would make a false statement in Bradina at that time?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I really do not know what his character is. I do not know what he would say and what he would say about other people and to whom he would say it. I really do not know.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: If someone were to describe you as a "defender from Bradina", you would quarrel with that description, would you not? You would say that was not true.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Whoever knows me can describe me and why could not he describe me? It is not impossible.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: If someone said you were a defender of Bradina in the context of a military operation, that would not be true, would it?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Let me tell you something, I was not in a position to defend the village, my house, Bradina. If there were military formations, if we had weapons and if we had the strength, we certainly would have defended it and succeeded in defending it. I do not know what you expect me to say. Am I here put on trial? Am I being accused for being at home, for being captured for having spent time in the camp. I simply do not understand this.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: What is being done is you are being asked questions on cross-examination. I am not accusing you of anything, do you understand that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No. That is how I feel.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: My job is to ask you questions and your job is to answer them. I am not accusing you of anything. I am trying to find out what you are going to say when I ask these questions. That is what cross-examination is.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I am doing my best to answer the gentleman as clearly as possible and with as many details so as to make myself clear. Maybe I am not literate enough to explain things as I would like them to be explained.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: I think you are doing fine, okay. I want to go to Celebici now, and I want to take you to the time that you were confined in tunnel nine during that first 110 days, okay?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: Now, the first thing I want to ask you about is the way you were seated there in tunnel nine. It is true, is it not, that the person seated right close to the door, the first position in the tunnel was Desimir Mrkajic?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: As far as I can remember, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: Then as you come further into the tunnel there is he will bother Mrkajic, Brane Mrkajic, Ratko Kuljanin, Momir Mrkajic Nikola Mrkajic and then you. You were number 7, right?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I think so.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: And then number eight was Andelko Kuljanin, then number nine, further into the tunnel, was a person named Sreten Zelenovic; correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I think so.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: Now anything that happened near or right outside that front door, I think you would agree with me that the person who had the best opportunity to observe what was happening would have been Desimir Mrkajic, since he was sitting right at the front door. Do you agree with that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I do. I agree.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: You have described for this Court a beating of Slavko Susic just outside that door; correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, when he was tortured by Zenga in front of the door.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: Your claim to this Court is that one of the persons who was beating him was Zenga, Senad Landzo; correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, that is what I said and I am repeating it now, one of them.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: Yes, one of them. There was also Osman Dedic, Focak, Nervin Zilic; right?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I did not mention Osman Dedic and the other man in the context of Susic, I only mentioned Landzo and Delic because I saw that it was them who tortured him. These other people may have tortured him in front of the Command building, but I did not see that. I am talking about people I saw torturing him.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: You deny then that you told Mr. Hortemo in the statement that you gave Mr. Hortemo that: "I watched Azim Delic; Senad Landzo, nicknamed 'Zenga'; Osman Dedic; someone called Focak and Nervin Zilic beat him." Are you saying you did not tell that to Mr. Hortemo?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: As far as I remember, I did not say that about Dedic and the other people that you listed. I did say about Osman when I was being beaten that he was there, and as regards Susic, I only mentioned Delic and Landzo.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: So this is another one of those statements that you want to say in spite of your signature on it that what you said in that statement was also not true?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, I really do not recall having stated that. Perhaps I did, perhaps I did something else in mind, but I really cannot say that they participated in it because they did not.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: Of course it is your contention before this Tribunal that when that beating of Slavko Susic was going on outside the door of tunnel number nine, the door was open so that you could see what was happening, that is your position, is it not?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: Do you have any idea why it would be that your acquaintance Desimir Mrkajic would say that the door was closed and that he could only hear what was going on outside?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That is not true. I do not know what he stated and when he stated what he had state. I really have no idea, but I know full well and I saw it with my own eyes because the door was open, that Landzo was torturing him. I saw Landzo torture him in front of the door and I saw what he was doing to him. It was not only me. There was other prisoners who saw this with their own eyes. If only Desimir Mrkajic is to be believed, that is not that.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: Okay, is that all you want to say about that? I take it your position is --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I said everything regarding Susic, everything that I had seen and everything that I lived through.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: Is your position that if Desimir Mrkajic was to have told someone that, that he is wrong; correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: There was some other people there apart from Desimir Mrkajic who saw what happened and other people should be asked what happened.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: That was not my question. The question was if Desimir Mrkajic told that, that would be wrong, that would be your position, would it not?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, absolutely.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: I would like the usher to show you a photograph now. This is a photograph from I think Prosecution Exhibit 1. I believe it is photograph number 50. It is this one right in the very back of the book (indicating). I think during direct examination you described that photograph as showing a pole that you were tied to during a time you were beaten by various persons. Could you show us again which of those poles it was you claimed to have been tied to. Point to it, not on the screen but on the ELMO, please.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Just let me say this, then I will show you. I do not have a sufficiently clear photograph as regards the poles themselves. They are original and that is the kind of poles that I was tied to. I believe that they are quite near tunnel number nine, quite near the tunnel. The photograph is not quite clear, but I believe that these are the poles in front of tunnel number nine, right adjacent to it in fact.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: Look at the photograph sitting on the ELMO. Turn round and look at it directly. It is a much clearer photograph and it may help if you see it over there. Do not look on the screen, look at the actual photograph.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: As regards the poles, they are familiar and the image is clear. They are those poles and I believe that they are right next to the tunnel, right on the tunnel.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: Were you tied to more than one of those poles by your statement, or not?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I was tied to one of them, as I only have two hands.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: Can you tell us which one?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I cannot tell you exactly which one. One of these two poles it was.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: Would it be one of the thicker ones or one of the narrower ones; do you know that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I do not know that either. I do not know. I was in no situation to really register precisely the type of pole I was tied to because I had been beaten and I was being beaten. I was really shocked when I saw them bringing a rope to tie me with. In fact I thought at the moment I would be hanged.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: Were you tied to that pole with your back to the pole with your hands behind you round the pole; is that the way you were tied to the pole?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: My hands were around the pole and I was facing the pole.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: Were you tied loosely to the pole or tightly to the pole?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I was tied tightly to it. My hands were tied tightly and I was also gagged with some sort of a rag.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: The people who you have told us were involved in this incident were Senad Landzo, Camdzic and Zilic; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Landzo was there, he tied me to the pole, and Osman Dedic, Camdzic and I do not know. There was another one. I do not know who it was.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: If you told Mr. Hortemo of the office of the prosecutor that it was a person name Zilic, or something like that, does that refresh your memory?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It could have been him. I really did not remember well, cannot remember well the names of the guard. I remember their faces better.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: You were beaten for approximately 45 minutes while tied around that pole; correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: All I can say exactly to a minute or 10 minutes. It lasted about half an hour, perhaps 45 minutes. I cannot say precisely.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: And you were beaten by, beaten on the back and beaten in the kidney area, that sort of thing?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, and in the head after having been ordered to kneel, and I kneeled there as they hit me. When they stopped I could not walk.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: Can you tell me approximately how many times you were hit while you were in that position?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Not only if I had someone in charge to count the blows and tell me afterwards I could do that. I really have no idea how many times I have been hit. I only know how I ended and how I felt afterwards.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: So prior to being tied to that pole you had already been beaten prior to that so you were in pretty bad shape before that beating even began, was that your position?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Certainly I was beaten before and beaten severely.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: So you are tied to this pole with your head up against the pole and four people standing behind you beating you, I take it you cannot tell us who it was that hit you with each of those blows. You were not able to see who it was that was hitting you; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I saw these persons when I left the tunnel number nine when Zenga placed a rifle barrel to my head. Then he also brandished this rope. He had this rope with which he tied me to the pole. First he said they would hang me, but they did not. They tied me up to the pole and they beat me and Dedic, as I already said, Osman and Camdzic were with Zenga on that occasion and another man whose name I cannot recall.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: Yes, I understand all that, but that was not my question. It is probably that I asked it wrong. Let me try is it again. At the time the blows were being struck, you are not able to tell this Tribunal who it was that struck each of those blows, which one of those four. You just know that someone among those four people was beating you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: All of them were beating me, certainly all them hit me.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: That is just an assumption on your part because you could not see who was hitting you because you were lashed to a pole and could not swivel your head round backwards and watch, could you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, I could not turn my head and watch them beating me.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: All right. Now it is true -- excuse me just a second, your Honour. You were at Celebici when the International Committee of the Red Cross came the first time; correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: And you know that by that time Mr. Landzo had already left Celebici and was there no longer?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That is not true.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: Do you know of an organisation by the name of the Association of Detainees?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: Are you a member of any organisation called the Association of Detainees in Belgrade?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, I am not.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: You have never been to their offices?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, I have not.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: Never talked to anyone there?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I have never talked to anyone from such an association. I do not know of any such association. I do not know what their function or their task is.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: Prior to your coming here to give your testimony, aside from the three statements that we have talked about, have you talked with anyone outside The Hague with any kind of an observation or association about your experiences and given them any kind of statements?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, I know of no association. I have not talked to anyone apart from this here final.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: How about the Serbian Council Information Centre; does that ring any bells with you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, it does not.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: Do you know a gentleman by the name of Petar Fjodovan?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It is the first time I heard of it.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: Branka Jovanovic?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: Can you remind me of the date that you claimed to have escaped from Musala?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I believe that it was 3rd November 1993.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: And Relja Mrkajic that was with you was not the Dr Relja Mrkajic, was it?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, it was not.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: That is all the questions I have, thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: You are welcome.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI-WHYTE
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Any other cross-examination?

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Your Honours, it is my turn for the cross-examination now.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI-WHYTE
utterances.text: Yes, you may proceed.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: May I proceed?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI-WHYTE
utterances.text: Yes, you may.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Kuljanin, you must be tired after this whole day of questioning, but before I start with my questions I should like to tell you something that you probably know. I am defendant's counsel for Mr. Zejnil Delalic and since I am the first person to be putting questions to you who speaks and understands your language and you understand mine, I would like by warning you to warn myself too that we bear in mind that what I am asking and what you are answering is being translated, so that in order to make it possible for their Honours and everyone else here in the courtroom to be able to follow, I ask you to wait for my question to be translated, to give your answer and I will wait for the translation of your answer. It may seem to us to be rather slow, this process of question and answer, but that is the only possible procedure. Have you understood what I am saying. Yes, thank you thank you. Mr. Kuljanin, in the course of the examination in chief by the prosecution you gave some information regarding your work, what you did and where you worked. I would just like to ask whether as a caterer or rather as a waiter, were you working at Stojcevac until the beginning of the war, that is in the Hotels Igman, the work organisation of the winter Olympic games; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: In 1985 I completed the catering school in Sarajevo and in 1986 I think it was, that the first time that I went to Bjeljasinca mountain where you worked in the Hotel Smok. Afterwards, as necessary, I was transferred to Hotel Igman, as all those hotels belonged to a single company, Stojcevac, Igman and Bjeljasinca. I would be sent where I was needed. So I cannot tell you exactly where I worked at what time as regards those three hotels.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: But in any event until the beginning of the war you worked in the various facilities belonging to this organisation as a waiter?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, but more recently towards the end I was on holiday. I had some days off, but in any event all my documents were left there in the company in Sarajevo. Whether any of that was recovered, I do not know.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Kuljanin, since we have only just started the cross-examination let me repeat again the warning I made. You understand me and you are answering me immediately but you can hear the English translation and only when you hear the end of the translation will you then answer.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, I really do not listen to the translation.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: I can already see that the questions and answers are getting blended together.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I can only hear you.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Will you please pay attention because on these other earphones you will be able to hear the English translation of my question. When that translation comes to an end will you answer me then and I will continue with my questions? In view of the fact that you said that you had worked in several facilities belonging to the same company, the winter Olympic games, as it was called, can you tell the court that these facilities, Stojcevac, Igman were facilities close to the city of Sarajevo, or rather on the territory of the municipalities belonging to the city of Sarajevo; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, that is correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: And for the last five or six years you were mostly living in those same facilities in which you worked, you were temporarily accommodated there, whereas on weekends and on your free days you went home to Bradina; is that so?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: You went to work for the last time somewhere in April 1992; is that so?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I think so. I think that is so.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: And then you returned from your work safely to Bradina, where you stayed until the combat operations that you have been testifying about all day today?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I was in Bradina.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: From your place of work in Stojcevac or Mount Igman you went to Bradina and reached Bradina safely without any problems; is that so?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: At that time as a citizen of both Sarajevo and Bradina you knew that the situation in the city of Sarajevo was very difficult after the events of April 6th; is that so?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: May I just say that I was in Bradina before April 6th. I reached Bradina, I cannot recall the exact date, but it was before April 6th.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: As a citizen of Bradina you were monitoring what was happening in Sarajevo after the proclaimation of Bosnia Herzegovina?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: And as a citizen of Konjic and Bosnia Herzegovina you knew that because of those events a state of immediate threat of war had been introduced in Bosnia Herzegovina?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: And you know as a military conscript that that state means that a work obligation is being introduced on a footing of equality with a military obligation and that employed people were duty bound to go to work?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: In spite of that, Mr. Kuljanin, you did not go to work, nor did you report to your work organisation or company to receive other military assignment; is that so?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It is.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: As you were born in Konjic and that is your permanent residence, you were also aware that after this proclaimation of general mobilisation you should have reported to the military department of the municipal community of Konjic?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: You stayed in Bradina. You did not report to the territorial defence of the Konjic municipality?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, that is so.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Since under your military obligations you may also be appointed to the reserve police force you did not report to the MUP of the city of Konjic, did you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I did not.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI-WHYTE
utterances.text: You are quite correct, this is a convenient time to break. Quite right. We will continue tomorrow morning.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honours. (The court adjourned) 17 18 19 20 21 22 23 24 25
